Sports.title: Guimaraes makes bow and Lewis-Skelly scores as Arsenal held by Como
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimaraes made his first appearance and Myles Lewis-Skelly scored amid speculation about his future as Arsenal were held to a 1-1 draw by Como before winning 4-3 on penalties.

Guimaraes, a £75m signing from Newcastle, was introduced at half-time in the pre-season friendly at the Emirates Stadium after Lewis-Skelly's opener had been cancelled out by Martin Baturina.

Lewis-Skelly's goal, stroked home after cutting out a poor pass from Como goalkeeper Jean Butez, came as he is linked with an Arsenal exit. He celebrated by making a heart gesture with his hands.

Guimaraes received a warm welcome with his introduction but Arsenal were unable to find a second-half winner before emerging victorious in the post-match penalty shoot-out in which Guimaraes and fellow new signing Christos Tzolis were among the scorers.

Image: Arsenal's Bruno Guimaraes came on at half-time

Mikel Arteta left out Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice and Martin Zubimendi despite their returns from World Cup duty this week, but there were first cameos of pre-season from their England and Spain team-mates Eberechi Eze, David Raya, Mikel Merino and Noni Madueke.

Arsenal's attention now turns to Sunday's Community Shield against Manchester City at Wembley before their Premier League curtain-raiser against Coventry, live on Sky Sports, on Friday August 21.

The key moments from the Emirates Stadium

7: CHANCE! Gabriel Jesus misses a sitter as his shot hits the post when it appeared easier to score.

Gabriel Jesus misses a sitter as his shot hits the post when it appeared easier to score. 21: SAVE! Martin Baturina cuts inside from the left flank and forces a low save from Kepa Arrizabalaga.

Martin Baturina cuts inside from the left flank and forces a low save from Kepa Arrizabalaga. 33: GOAL! Myles Lewis-Skelly punishes an error from Como goalkeeper Jean Butez as he strokes home the opener

Myles Lewis-Skelly punishes an error from Como goalkeeper Jean Butez as he strokes home the opener 43: GOAL! Como pull level as Baturina dances between Theo Julienne and Max Dowman before firing home an emphatic finish.

Como pull level as Baturina dances between Theo Julienne and Max Dowman before firing home an emphatic finish. 46: WELCOME! Bruno Guimaraes is welcomed by the home fans as he is introduced at half-time for his first Gunners appearance.

Bruno Guimaraes is welcomed by the home fans as he is introduced at half-time for his first Gunners appearance. 53 WASTE! Martin Odegaard puts a chance on a plate for Fabio Vieira but his shot is saved.

Martin Odegaard puts a chance on a plate for Fabio Vieira but his shot is saved. PENALTIES! Arsenal win the shoot-out 4-3 with Guimaraes among the scorers and Noni Madueke the only player to miss.

Analysis: Salmon shows star potential

The debut of a £75m signing and a goal from the player who may have to make way for his arrival took the headlines, but the performance from Marli Salmon provided another talking point.

One of two Arsenal 16-year-olds to start the game along with Max Dowman, the defender was outstanding, his performance a continuation of a strong pre-season.

He lined up at centre-back, with another teenager, the 18-year-old Theo Julienne, as his full-back, but as Arteta made sweeping substitutions and the personnel around him changed, Salmon remained calm and consistent, earning a standing ovation from fans inside the ground when he finally came off in the 88th minute.

Image: Marli Salmon and Mikel Arteta

Salmon departed having won nine of his 13 duels, the most of any player on either side. He had also completed 42 of his 43 passes, which was, again, a game high. The numbers reflected his confidence and quality both in and out of possession.

Como head coach Cesc Fabregas, himself a former Arsenal academy prodigy, marvelled at his impact alongside Dowman. "Amazing. That's what it's all about. Hale End does an amazing job," he said. And there was also praise from Arteta, who appears to have another credible defensive option. "I think he was exceptional," he said.

Arteta: Bruno was pushing to play

Manager Mikel Arteta on Bruno Guimaraes in his press conference: "He only had three training sessions, but he looked good.

"He was really pushing to play some minutes today.

"I think he wanted to get his debut and the feeling of playing in front of our fans immediately.

"And, yeah, you sense immediately, I believe, a strong connection at play that is going to make us better."

Merino: We're ready for 'another final'

Arsenal midfielder Mikel Merino speaking to Arsenal's official YouTube channel: "I think we dominated. The team showed what it is capable of.

"Everyone was in a good level. Honestly, I think we deserved to win; we had massive chances to score.

"We take the positives into the next game and hopefully we can dominate every game like we did today."

On the Community Shield: "It's another final and we want to win, we want to give the fans more happiness.

"But especially for us, we want to compete. Wearing this shirt and this badge means a lot and that's about giving everything and playing to our best capacity."

Sports.title: Arteta: There's more we want to do in the transfer market
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta says Arsenal are actively looking for more new signings in the transfer market but admits there is only a small pool of available players who can take them to the next level.

The Gunners were frustrated in their attempts to land Vinicius Junior, who chose to sign a new contract at Real Madrid, and also missed out on the signing of another top target Morgan Rogers, who joined Chelsea from Aston Villa earlier this summer.

Arsenal completed the £75m signing of Bruno Guimaraes on Saturday, with the Brazil international making his first appearance for the club in Wednesday's friendly against Como at the Emirates Stadium, but their efforts to add firepower are ongoing.

"There is more that we want to do because every time we have an opportunity to improve the squad and bring more quality and depth to the squad, we need to do that," said Arteta.

"We are actively trying to do so. The thing in the market is that it doesn't just depend on you. We are very clear on that.

"But the approach, the will and the desire of the club, that's unquestionable. We want to try to do that. But we cannot promise that we're going to do it because it doesn't only depend on us."

The Premier League champions are interested in Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez and Paris Saint-Germain's Bradley Barcola but their search for a marquee attacking signing appears set to continue deep into the transfer window.

"I think for the margins to improve, there are very few players in the market that are available to do that and bring that to the club," added Arteta.

"But again, we are actively looking to improve that and we're going to try."

Asked if Arsenal's wage structure could be affected by signings of that stature, Arteta added: "I'll leave that question to [sporting director] Andrea [Berta] and the board.

"My job is more to focus on getting the best out of the players that we have, to create that connection between them and to make every player feel important, regardless of the wages."

'Bruno was pushing to play'

Arteta was pleased to hand a debut to Guimaraes against Como, as he impressed as a half-time substitute only four days after his arrival from Newcastle and could now be in contention to start in Sunday's Community Shield against Manchester City.

Image: Arsenal's Bruno Guimaraes featured in the second half against Como

"Let's see," said Arteta. "He only had three training sessions, but he looked good. He was really pushing to play some minutes.

"I think he wanted to get his debut and the feeling of playing in front of our fans immediately.

"And you sense immediately, I believe, a strong connection at play that is going to make us better."

Arteta coy on Lewis-Skelly future

Myles Lewis-Skelly has been linked with a departure from Arsenal following the arrival of Guimaraes. He was the subject of an enquiry from Chelsea and is also a long-term target for Manchester United.

But the 19-year-old scored Arsenal's goal against Como, after which he made a heart gesture before holding his hands together towards the home fans.

Image: Myles Lewis-Skelly gestured to Arsenal fans after his goal

"It's good to score a goal, you should be emotional when you score a goal," said Arteta of his celebration. "He's a very emotional player. I remember when he did all the gestures on the pitch [last season]. I'm not going to talk about any speculation.

"If there is a speculation about our player, it's a good sign. That means that we attract attention and they're doing a good job.

"I think he had a really good pre-season. I think we asked him to play in a different position, because he played more as a six, because we lacked central midfielders, obviously with international duties, and I think he had a really consistent pre-season."

Sports.title: Chelsea set Man City deadline to bid for Fernandez
Sports.content:
Chelsea have told Manchester City they have a deadline of 5pm this Friday to make an offer for Enzo Fernandez.

City are interested in the midfielder, who shared a strong relationship with Enzo Maresca when he was Chelsea boss.

Chelsea value Fernandez at £120m and he has six years left on his contract.

If City do not meet Chelsea's demands, they do not intend to sell Fernandez in this window.

Barcelona's pursuit of Rodri - which saw them have a £40m bid rejected - has raised the prospect of Manchester City making a late move for Fernandez before the window closes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' Mark McAdam with the latest on Rodri's potential move to LaLiga side Barcelona

City have targets in mind for any player who departs and they are in ongoing talks with Lille for Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi. They have already signed central-midfielder Elliot Anderson for £116m from Nottingham Forest.

Chelsea have a high valuation for Fernandez but they signed him for around £107m from Benfica in the 2023 winter window. The summer transfer window closes on Tuesday September 1.

Relations between City and Chelsea are strained after the acrimonious manner of Maresca's departure from Chelsea.

City paid Chelsea £17m in compensation to appoint Maresca this summer. He had resigned with three and a half years to run on his contract at the end of 2025 after being sounded out about succeeding Pep Guardiola last autumn.

Chelsea chose to impose this deadline to avoid the distractions that arose when Maresca stood down with his shock exit announced by the club on New Year's Day.

Their view is that interested clubs have had the best part of two months to make an approach for Fernandez. They want new manager Xabi Alonso and his players to be able to focus on the new season ahead.

Fernandez was dropped by Chelsea for two games in April after he admitted he would welcome living in Madrid.

The player and his agent also apologised for his comments. They had been seeking improved terms at Chelsea.

Real Madrid released a statement earlier this summer denying that they would make an attempt to sign Fernandez.

Barcelona expected to raise bid for Rodri

Barcelona are ready to raise their offer for Rodri - which could lead to Man City making their move for Fernandez before Chelsea's deadline.

City want to keep the 30-year-old but he has entered the final year of his contract.

Barcelona are ready to up their offer to City for Rodri to somewhere in the £50m (€60m) to £60m (€70m) bracket.

City are also aware of interest from Nottingham Forest in Tijjani Reijnders.

Sports.title: Atletico agree deal to sign Spurs captain Romero
Sports.content:
Atletico Madrid have agreed a deal in principle with Tottenham to sign Cristian Romero.

The package is in the region of £34.2m (€40m) with add-ons. A 15 per cent sell-on clause is included.

Atletico have been long-term admirers of the Argentina international, and there was an expectation that Spurs would allow captain Romero to depart this summer if the right offer arrived.

The central defender was always believed to have preferred a move to Atletico, with Inter Milan and Spurs' north London rivals Arsenal among the other clubs to have been interested.

Romero's Spurs deal is due to run until the summer of 2029.

The 28-year-old was sent off twice last season during Spurs' Premier League relegation battle. He then missed the end of the campaign due to a knee injury.

Romero received criticism from supporters when he appeared to be set to watch his boyhood club Belgrano play River Plate in the Argentina Primera Division Apertura final instead of being at Tottenham's crucial last game against Everton. Romero did, though, attend the final game of the season, in which Spurs secured Premier League survival.

He has made 124 appearances for the club over five seasons, scoring 12 goals and being shown four red cards in the Premier League.

Spurs had appeared to lay the groundwork for Romero's exit this summer following the arrivals of defenders Jan Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi.

'Spurs not getting value for Romero'

Spurs are set to take a lower fee for Romero than what they received for teenage defender Luka Vuskovic, who joined Brighton in a club-record £50m deal earlier this summer.

Speaking on Sky Sports' Tottenham summer special podcast, which will be available to listen to from midday on Thursday, Sky Sports News' Michael Bridge said of Romero's imminent exit: "Spurs are not going to get the value for a player of his ability.

"Luka Vuskovic, who didn't make any competitive appearances for Spurs, will be sold for more than what the club's captain will go for because he's gone to a Premier League club.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Romero's last game for Spurs ended in tears as he suffered a season-ending injury in the loss at Sunderland

"I think it's best for all parties that Romero leaves. I think 99.9 per cent of Spurs fans would agree with that.

"On his day, there aren't many better - he doesn't make any mistakes for Argentina, but in terms of Tottenham it just feels like it's his job.

"He adores Argentina, and there's nothing wrong with that, but it feels as if Tottenham is a bit of a chore for him and it's gone a bit too much that way."

Could Romero have joined Arsenal?

Earlier this month, one source had told Sky Sports News that Arsenal had looked into Romero as an option to bolster their centre-back options.

However, it never progressed beyond interest, with Spurs reluctant to let their captain join a Premier League side, let alone their fiercest rivals Arsenal.

"There was talk that Romero would have happily accepted a move to Arsenal," Bridge told Sky Sports' Tottenham summer special podcast.

"There were no club-to-club talks on this, but when you hear that then that's the final nail for Tottenham supporters."

The north London rivals tend not to do transfer business with one another. The last transfer negotiated between the two clubs came 49 years ago when goalkeeper Pat Jennings joined Arsenal from Spurs in a deal worth a reported £45,000.

O'Hara: Time for Romero to move on

Also speaking on Sky Sports' Tottenham summer special podcast, ex-Spurs midfielder Jamie O'Hara said of Romero: "He's a bit of a liability. When he plays, he costs us games, points and red cards.

"I just think his attitude towards the board and the way he was, I just think it's, 'All right, thank you, and we're going to move on'.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie O'Hara called for Tottenham to sell Romero

"We've finished 17th the last two seasons, and he's been involved. He was captain last season, and the way he acted at the end of the season, when he got injured, and we all saw him crying, that wasn't for Tottenham; it was more for Argentina and his World Cup.

"And then he goes to Argentina on the last day of the season, and everyone's like, 'Where's Romero?' So that situation for me needs to be put to bed. I don't think we need any of that bad publicity around us.

"Get as much as we can for him; let him move on. We've got back-up now with Van Hecke and Senesi, so thank you, see you later."

Spurs are set to make a loss on Romero, who joined from Atalanta for around £42m in the summer of 2021.

O'Hara said of Atletico's £34.2m deal for Romero: "The problem is there's a premium for English clubs, who will pay over the odds for people with European clubs inflating the fee.

"The problem is if you're going to go and sell him to Atletico Madrid, they haven't got the money.

"If we were selling him to Man Utd, we could probably get £60m-70m for him. But the problem is if you sell a player to Europe, they just don't have the money that the Premier League clubs have, so you have to accept that it's going to be a lesser fee than what maybe you think you can get for him.

"He wants to go to Atletico Madrid. He just feels like an Atletico Madrid player. I just feel like you've just got to take that one on the chin and move on from it."

Romero's exit signals new era at Spurs

Image: Romero is set to leave Spurs after five years at the club

Speaking on Sky Sports' Tottenham summer special podcast, Sky Sports News senior football news editor Lyall Thomas said:

"Quite a top figure in the football industry said to me, 'Go and watch Romero's role in the second goal in Spurs' 3-0 defeat to Nottingham Forest at home last season'.

"I watched him, and it was arms in the air, not tracking the player back who ended up scoring, which contributed to the goal.

"That was Spurs when they needed their captain the most, and he just wasn't there in that moment, so that says it all.

"It's time to move on from that era of Spurs and into the new era.

"This has been shown by some of the players they've brought in, which is not just to have an impact on the field but to have an impact on the dressing room and sort that area of the club.

"It's a move that suits Romero to go and work with his compatriot [Diego] Simeone. I can imagine they will suit each other down to the ground. It just fits. The planets are aligned on this one."

Sports.title: Doue silences Madjo-mania as PSG beat Villa to win Super Cup
Sports.content:
Desire Doue scored the winner as champions of Europe Paris Saint-Germain beat Aston Villa 2-1 to win the UEFA Super Cup.

The 21-year-old raced in behind the defence and restored the lead for the Ligue 1 side to ensure they retained the trophy but Villa went down swinging in what was a highly-contested fixture at the Red Bull Arena in Salzburg.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia had initially given PSG the lead after cutting inside from the left and wrong-footing Marco Bizot with his well-taken effort (20) but a goal on his professional debut for 17-year-old Brian Madjo sparked Villa into life.

The forward became the youngest player to score in the Super Cup after shrugging off the challenge from Willian Pacho to volley the equaliser home and arguably should have had more to his name, having seen three other chances sail just wide of the target.

Image: Brian Madjo of Aston Villa celebrates scoring against PSG

Villa were without key players Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa and Emiliano Martinez due to their extended post-World Cup breaks but the gaps left by senior players provided the likes of Madjo and 19-year-old George Hemmings with a platform to shine.

The two teenagers looked at home among world-class opposition and the latter came close to responding to Doue's strike seconds after Villa conceded, only for Matvey Safonov to make a fine stop to deny him.

Image: Desire Doue celebrates after scoring what proved the winner for PSG against Aston Villa in the UEFA Super Cup

Luis Enrique's side would hold on to start the 2026/27 campaign with silverware but they were given an almighty scare by Unai Emery and his new-look squad, in a similar fashion to the 5-4 thriller that played out in the Champions League when the sides last met in 2025.

The key moments from Red Bull Arena Salzburg

20: GOAL! Kvaratskhelia opens the scoring for PSG

Kvaratskhelia opens the scoring for PSG 28: CLOSE! Madjo's header curls just wide of the target

Madjo's header curls just wide of the target 35: MADJO MISSES! Another shot from the young striker whistles just wide

Another shot from the young striker whistles just wide 41: MADJO HAS TO SCORE! Madjo's header balloons over the bar from close range

Madjo's header balloons over the bar from close range 45: FINALLY! Madjo makes history and becomes youngest Super Cup goalscorer

Madjo makes history and becomes youngest Super Cup goalscorer 62: GOAL! Doue restores PSG lead

Doue restores PSG lead 64: SAVE! Hemmings has chance to equalise but Safonov saves

Emery: We must feel proud of this performance

Aston Villa boss Unai Emery speaking to TNT Sports:

"With a loss, you can never feel happy but how we compete, how the players respond on the field for 90 minutes. And our chances to score, we must feel really very proud of what we have done today."

On the performances of Brian Madjo and George Hemmings: "Their experiences and having days like today are very important.

"They show how are they are learning after their hard work. This is the way. We decided before the game how we wanted to play this game; we have worked the players in these positions."

Sports.title: Doué seals Super Cup glory for PSG after Madjo makes history for Villa
Sports.content:
Luis Enrique says it doesn’t matter which sport he is playing – football, tennis, padel or parchis, a board game – he wants to win all of the time. In Paris Saint-Germain, he has built a winning machine, the back-to-back Champions League victors maintaining a useful habit by conquering Aston Villa in an absorbing Super Cup contest in Salzburg. For PSG, after the joy of Munich and Budapest, three months ago, does a three-peat in Madrid in May beckon?

Aston Villa more than played their part in an enthralling showpiece, Brian Madjo becoming the competition’s youngest scorer after the 17-year-old cancelled out Khvicha Kvaratskhelia’s opener. They could have taken the game to a penalty shootout, Warren Zaïre-Emery’s extraordinary block preventing João Gomes a near-certain debut goal and Emi Buendía heading wide in stoppage time.

Villa will take plenty of encouragement from a fearless display, Désiré Doué’s well-taken winner ultimately the difference. The goal was initially disallowed but, after a VAR review, Omar Artan – the Somali referee handed the game by Uefa after being denied entry to the US to officiate at the World Cup – awarded it after replays showed Matty Cash played Doué onside.

Before kick-off, the sights and sounds were in effect an extension of Villa’s victory in Istanbul, a party atmosphere raining down from the 6,000-strong Villa following. There were huge cheers when Unai Emery’s face appeared on the big screens in opposite corners after the teams were read aloud and hearty roars for the £38m arrival Gomes and Madjo, the hulking forward who made his presence felt on his full Villa debut. Madjo’s inclusion felt particularly ominous for Tammy Abraham, the striker signed seven months ago, his £18.25m arrival yet to pay dividends.

“We won’t be in our best moment,” Emery warned on the eve of the game but, after a summer of change, the future looks bright. Emery could finally unleash Madjo in a competitive game for the first time since his £10m arrival from Metz in January, Villa winning an appeal at the court of arbitration for sport (Cas) to register him after Fifa prohibited him from playing. Chelsea’s João Pedro is the only Premier League player to have outscored Madjo in pre-season and his equaliser here was on the grandest stage yet after goals against Walsall, Real Sociedad and Indonesia All Stars. Madjo occupied Willian Pacho and Marquinhos, one of the most decorated defenders in the world. The 19-year-old George Hemmings played the full game and kept Achraf Hakimi on his toes.

Only five players from Villa’s memorable victory over Freiburg remained in the XI though Emi Martínez, Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins are still on holiday. Emery told Watkins to rest after the striker volunteered to play here. Boubacar Kamara made his first start since sustaining a serious knee injury against Tottenham in January. More new faces will join, with Villa in advanced talks to sign João Palhinha from Bayern Munich and the Atlético Madrid left-back Matteo Ruggeri expected to undergo a medical in the next 48 hours. “Overall we can feel proud of everything we’ve done,” Emery said. “Some changes will be needed but we are confident.”

View image in fullscreen Brian Madjo punches the air after scoring for Aston Villa on the stroke of half-time. Photograph: Angelika Warmuth/Reuters

PSG seized the lead on 20 minutes through Kvaratskhelia, who had the summer off. Madjo’s clunky control allowed Vitinha to claim the ball and locate Doué. Then Kvaratskhelia took charge, jinking inside Cash and blasting his shot in at Marco Bizot’s near post. Six minutes later, it should have been 2-0 after more Kvaratskhelia brilliance, but PSG could not apply the finishing touch. Nuno Mendes galloped on to Kvaratskhelia’s flipped pass but the full-back’s cutback from the left flank evaded the £43m summer buy Maghnes Akliouche and three other blue and red shirts.

Madjo had a hat-trick of chances from John McGinn’s cunning crosses before levelling. He glanced at the screens showing a replay of him misdirecting a free header. Then he overcooked a shot when looking for the far corner after Hemmings beat Hakimi. Another flunked header followed after McGinn twirled clear of Kvaratskhelia. But with the half-time whistle looming, Madjo made amends, dispatching a side-footed volley into the roof of Matvey Safonov’s net after meeting another brilliant cross from McGinn. As the ball flew towards the back post, Pacho clung to Madjo for dear life, but the teenager kept him at arm’s length to ripple the net.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Ousmane Dembélé replaced Akliouche at half-time. Fabián Ruiz, the only other player missing from the XI that began against Arsenal in Budapest in May, arrived late on. Villa kept hunting, McGinn working Safonov after Madjo spread play. But PSG regained the lead just after the hour when Dembélé’s pass unlocked Villa’s defence, exposing an imperfect offside line. Dembélé zipped the ball into the right channel and, while Ian Maatsen and Pau Torres raised their hands and Doué’s goal was initially ruled out, semi-automated offside exposed Cash.

Villa still had chances to level. Zaïre-Emery slid across the turf to thwart Gomes. Safonov repelled Hemmings’s strike from close range and the substitutes Alysson and Abraham almost combined to devastating effect but Abraham did not gamble in the box, much to Emery’s frustration. Perhaps Villa will, as McGinn suggested this week, prove everybody wrong – again.

Sports.title: Atlético Madrid agree £34.1m deal for Tottenham’s Cristian Romero
Sports.content:
Tottenham have reached an agreement with Atlético Madrid over the sale of captain Cristian Romero.

Romero was given the green light by the club and Roberto De Zerbi to depart Spurs this summer after a turbulent 2025-26 campaign where he served four separate suspensions.

Inter initially led the chase for the Argentina centre-back, but after talks with Spurs stalled, long-term admirers Atlético swooped in and a package of €40m (£34.1m) is set to secure Diego Simeone his target.

It will bring a rollercoaster five-year spell in north London to an end for Romero, who joined in 2021 and enjoyed mixed success under Antonio Conte before a strong bond was formed with Ange Postecoglou.

Romero wore the captain’s armband when Tottenham ended a 17-year trophy drought with victory over Manchester United in the 2025 Europa League final and produced a fine performance to ensure Postecoglou’s promise of silverware in his second season came true.

However, Postecoglou’s dismissal weeks later was met with a thinly-veiled social media post in the direction of Spurs’ hierarchy by Romero and more followed during a chaotic last season where only a final-day win over Everton avoided relegation.

Romero, who was made captain by Thomas Frank ahead of the 2025-26 campaign, was in Argentina days before Tottenham’s 1-0 success over Everton to receive treatment on a knee injury before he got a flight back to be present in the stands.

The return of Romero for the relegation decider only occurred after widespread criticism from Spurs supporters and it proved the final nail in the coffin for many fans.

World Cup winner Romero will exit Spurs after 156 appearances and link up with compatriot Simeone, who has repeatedly talked up the quality of the Argentinian in recent seasons and will finally get his man this summer.

Tottenham have inserted a 15% sell-on clause in the deal and this imminent departure continues a summer of mass changes with De Zerbi overseeing a huge revamp of a squad which has finished 17th in consecutive seasons.

Newly-promoted Hull have broken their transfer record to sign Senegal defender Nobel Mendy from Spanish side Rayo Vallecano. They also signed Australia international Lucas Herrington on Wednesday.

View image in fullscreen Lucas Herrington became Australia’s youngest player to make a World Cup appearance this summer. Photograph: Alex Livesey/Fifa/Getty Images

The Tigers have not disclosed the fee for the 21-year-old Mendy but it exceeds the reported £20m they paid for Greece goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis last week.

Mendy, who has one international cap and previously played for Paris FC and Real Betis, has signed a five-year deal, with an option for a further 12 months.

He finished his only season with Rayo Vallecano with an appearance in May’s Conference League final loss to Crystal Palace.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“I have wanted to play in the Premier League since I was little, so it’s a great challenge to face and I am ready for it,” Mendy told Hull’s website.

Herrington, 18, became Australia’s youngest player to start a World Cup game for the Socceroos this summer, and arrived from MLS side Colorado Rapids on a five-year deal.

Crystal Palace have re-signed Aston Villa’s Evann Guessand on loan for the season with an option to buy. The Côte d’Ivoire international made 14 appearances after moving to Selhurst Park in January until the end of last season, but in July Palace opted against making the move permanent.

The 25-year-old joined Villa from Ligue 1 side Nice for £30m last summer but failed to win a regular place in Unai Emery’s side.

Celtic have signed Egypt winger Haissem Hassan from Spanish club Real Oviedo, subject to international clearance.

The 24-year-old, who impressed at this summer’s World Cup, joins the Scottish champions on a four-year deal, with the option of a further 12 months.

“When I heard about Celtic being interested in me, I had to get here and be part of the club,” Hassan told the club website. Manager Martin O’Neill said Celtic had done “really well” to secure a player of Hassan’s quality amid interest from other clubs.

“He is someone who I think has the ability and experience to do very well for us, performing at a high level in domestic and international football,” said O’Neill.

Sports.title: Anderson still pained by England defeat but ready to shine at Manchester City
Sports.content:
Elliot Anderson has admitted ­England’s World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina still pains him, but is hoping to use the confidence from his performances at the ­tournament to inspire the start of his Manchester City career.

Anderson will probably make his debut when City play ­the Premier League winners, Arsenal, on ­Sunday at the Principality ­Stadium in ­Cardiff for the Community Shield.

“It’s really hard,” Anderson said of England’s loss. “I’m still sort of ­struggling with that. There are highs and lows in football. It’s about how you bounce back.

“I’ve had three weeks to reflect on it, but now is a new season, you have to move forward.

I take huge confidence knowing I can perform on a World Cup stage. I hadn’t played in anything as big as that yet. That was a really good test for me.”

The 23-year-old is likely to become a significant figure in City midfield because of Barcelona’s interest in signing Rodri. A new £51m bid was made by the La Liga side on Wednesday, as they try to seal a deal for the 30-year-old. If the Ballon d’Or ­winner does depart, City’s new No 5 will be expected to be part of the plan to replace him in the middle of the park. Asked if he is similar in style to the Spaniard, Anderson said: “I think so. I can do various things within ­midfield and I’ll see where I get used.

“I’ll play anywhere. Creating things, driving forward or the other role if they ask me to do that.”

Anderson joined from Nottingham Forest for what was briefly a record £116m fee [Morgan Rogers’s £117m move to Chelsea soon eclipsed it] for a British player – City had a ­longstanding interest in him while Pep Guardiola was in charge. Due to his extended World Cup exertions with England, the former ­Newcastle midfielder is yet to feature for City under their new head coach, Enzo Maresca.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Guardiola’s departure, though, did not made him debate his decision. “It’s such a huge club and the players they have are the best. I want to be surrounded by these sorts of ­players, proving myself on a daily basis.

“[Kevin] De Bruyne was always the player I looked up to over the last 10 years. I loved watching him. To be here at the same club and playing where he played is special.”

Sports.title: Manchester United enjoy trip to Dublin with penalty shootout win over Leeds
Sports.content:
With blazing sunshine fading over a hot Dublin day, this penultimate friendly for Manchester United and Leeds United felt like a pre-season game on a far continent, not one staged a few hundred miles from the teams’ home across the Irish Sea.

The phoney-war element is always present whatever the locale, as ­players sharpen technique and fitness, so when Joshua Zirkzee’s instant left-foot shot met Diogo Dalot’s zipped-in cross and James Trafford saved low, all involved could be satisfied.

Even better for Michael Carrick’s men ensued: Bryan Mbeumo raced along the left and served the ball to Zirkzee who, again, hit a first-time effort that this time beat Trafford to his right.

Leeds had been scythed open, their right-side defenders, Jayden Bogle and Sebastiaan Bornauw, rendered awol by a lightning attack straight from the Carrick-Steve Holland ­training ground playbook.

Daniel Farke’s switch to a 3-5-2 at half-time of November’s 3-2 loss at Manchester City is credited, rightly, with saving their top-flight status, and the manager’s job.

Yet it can cause a retroactive-mode if the wingbacks retreat into a five-man rearguard. After Bogle and Rhys Chadwick did so, Mbeumo’s attempt, after one more United foray, underlined the problem.

More proactive, then, were two Ao Tanaka throw-ins that dipped into the area and posed those in red to scramble. When Leeds came straight back at them, a Tyler Fletcher shimmy backfired, and they profited.

The midfielder was robbed by Dan James who flipped the ball into the area where Brenden Aaronson stroked past Senne Lammens, who was helpless. So, too, Trafford when a Mbeumo rocket beat him, the bar saving Leeds, as, along the touchline, replacements prepared to enter for the second period.

Quick Guide Lewis-Skelly scores in Arsenal friendly as transfer speculation continues Show Myles Lewis-Skelly appeared to underline his commitment to Arsenal by setting aside transfer speculation to score in Wednesday’s 1-1 friendly draw with the Italian club Como. The 19-year-old has been linked with Chelsea and Manchester United amid uncertainty over his future. Starting in midfield, he capitalised on an error from the Como goalkeeper, Jean Butez, to put the hosts ahead in the 33rd minute at Emirates Stadium. Lewis-Skelly then made a heart sign to the crowd as he celebrated before tapping the club badge on his shirt on his way back to the centre circle. The England international signed a five-year contract with Arsenal last summer but his long-term future has come under scrutiny since he fell behind Riccardo Calafiori and Piero Hincapié last term to become Mikel Arteta’s third choice left-back. While he started only five Premier League games across the course of the campaign, he enjoyed an end-of-season resurgence in centre midfield. Arsenal, however, are well-stocked in that position after signing Bruno Guimarães to join Declan Rice, Martin Ødegaard and the World Cup winners Martín Zubimendi and Mikel Merino. Guimarães, who joined from Newcastle in a £75m deal, was introduced at half-time against Como to make his debut, while Lewis-Skelly was replaced in the 62nd minute by Merino. The Premier League champions were pegged back by Champions League-bound Como, who are managed by the former Arsenal midfielder Cesc Fàbregas, when Martin Baturina equalised in the 43rd minute. But Arsenal won the penalty shootout 4-3, with Guimarães and his fellow summer signing Christos Tzolis on target. PA Media Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Before the game, Carrick had issued an update on those not involved. “Marcus [Rashford], Licha [Martínez] and Kobbie [Mainoo] aren’t quite ready yet,” he said. “We’re ­preserving them for this weekend [against Milan in Wroclaw].”

Missing, too, were Mason Mount, as a precaution, Tom Heaton, whose problem is being assessed and Harry Maguire, who joined training on Wednesday.

“Tonight is going to be ­historical,” screeched the enthusiastic PA announcer when billing this ­inaugural meeting between two ­English clubs at the cavernous stadium.

View image in fullscreen Brenden Aaronson slots home Leeds’s first-half equaliser. Photograph: Stephen McCarthy/Sportsfile/Getty Images

But Carrick’s three half-time changes were hardly stellar names to please the capacity crowd. Off went Patrick Dorgu, Andrey Santos and Mbeumo for the fringe players, Toby Collyer, Daniel Armer, an 18-year-old debutant, and Tynan Thompson, given a first outing since joining recently.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Farke’s changes ran to 10, with only Bornauw surviving, so now the question was how disjointed the contest might be. Encouragingly, Harry ­Wilson and Alfie Cresswell tested Lammens, then slick Zirkzee footwork took him in on goal.

But further disruption followed when Carrick made six more changes, including the introduction of his captain, Bruno Fernandes, Youri Tielemans, his new £35m midfielder, and Matheus Cunha, who spearheaded the 4-2-3-1.

The result: a long lull before ­Lammens repelled a James Justin rasper, a Fernandes strike was ruled offside and the same player clipped the bar before penalties, to decide the Boyle Sports Cup, arrived.

Before the final whistle five fans rushed on for selfies with Fernandes and Tielemans – youngsters, sure, but a concerning security breach, ­especially as a sixth followed.

View image in fullscreen A capacity crowd of more than 80,000 turned up at Croke Park. Photograph: Stephen McCarthy/Sportsfile/Getty Images

United won the shootout 5-4, Noussair Mazraoui netting the decisive kick, and the teams wandered away offering scant clue how their 2026-27 season will be.

The pre-season results of United now read this victory, 1–1 against Paris Saint-Germain on Saturday, 2–1 (Atlético Madrid), 5–0 (Rosenborg) and the 1–0 loss to Wrexham on 18 July. After this defeat, Leeds’s record is 2-0, against RB Leipzig, 4-2 (Liverpool), 1-0 win (Sunderland), and the 3-2 defeat, also to Wrexham, on 26 July.

Leeds finish their preparation by hosting Augsburg, while United make the trip to Poland. Last term they ended third, 24 points ahead of Leeds in 14th. Given the former’s thus far underwhelming transfer window – only Tielemans and Santos as major signings – they would take the same finish, as would Leeds, surely, as survival will be their priority.

Sports.title: Xavi Hernández appointed head coach of the Netherlands on four-year contract
Sports.content:
The former Barcelona head coach Xavi Hernández has been appointed the new head coach of the Netherlands. The 46-year-old Spaniard has agreed a contract to lead the team through to the 2030 World Cup.

He replaces Ronald Koeman, who stepped down following the Netherlands’ last-32 defeat by Morocco at this summer’s World Cup.

Former Barcelona midfielder Xavi won the World Cup as a player with Spain in 2010 and also lifted the European Championship in 2008 and 2012. He guided Barça to the La Liga title in 2023 after beginning his managerial career with Qatari club Al Sadd.

“I consider it a tremendous honour to become head coach of the Dutch national team,” he said in a statement released by the Dutch Football Association (KNVB).

“As someone who received his training at the FC Barcelona academy, with strong influences from Johan Cruyff and Rinus Michels, among others, I feel a special connection to Dutch football. You could say that I am a bit of a son of Dutch football.”

Xavi’s appointment marks his first return to management since leaving Barcelona in 2024. He took over the Catalan club in November 2021, also succeeding Koeman, after making 767 appearances for the club.

“The Netherlands has a rich football culture and a clear vision that also appeals to me enormously: attacking football, based on possession, with creativity, passion, and conviction,” he said. “Of course, the most important goal is and always will be to win, but I prefer to do so in a way that reflects those characteristics and that people can enjoy. The potential for this is there, as well as a solid foundation to build upon.”

Former Liverpool head coach Arne Slot walked away from talks about replacing Koeman after saying he wants to remain in club football. His link to the role did not get beyond an initial approach.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“At this stage in my career, I prefer to see myself on the training pitch with my players every day, something that is simply not possible in the same way with a national team,” Slot told Voetbal International. “And [it is] why I chose not to continue the talks and not to start negotiations on what a possible contract might look like.

“I have enormous respect for the national team and for the KNVB [Dutch Football Association] and can only be positive about the professional manner in which the talks proceeded that week. For now, I believe club football still has a lot to offer me.”

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 6: Chelsea
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 3rd (NB: this is not necessarily Billy Munday’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 10th

Prospects

After a season of struggle and regression, with two head coaches and two spells under a caretaker, there is cautious optimism that this campaign will bring something like stability. Much of that optimism centres around the appointment of Xabi Alonso, an elite manager with something to prove. There is also an expectation that the young players brought in as part of BlueCo’s £1.8bn splurge in recent years are beginning to come into their best years. There is no European football to complicate the schedule and a return to the Champions League by finishing in the top four or five would suffice for now. More importance will be placed on the domestic cups after a season without trophies.

Alonso’s squad is more rounded than what Enzo Maresca or Liam Rosenior had at their disposal. Maxence Lacroix and Morgan Rogers bring quality to positions where Chelsea were lacking it – at centre-back and out wide. Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson – the “uncs” as Tosin Adarabioyo has called them – will contribute as much off the pitch as on it. The signing of Marco Palestra, a specialist wing-back, suggests Alonso wants to be tactically flexible. He has used a back four and a back three in pre-season.

What about Cole Palmer? For so much of his time at Stamford Bridge, Chelsea’s form has been tied to his. When he has struggled to be 100% fit, the team have suffered too. After being omitted from England’s World Cup squad, Palmer had a seven-week break and sought advice from a specialist on the groin injury that hampered him last season. “I got bored after six weeks,” Palmer said after returning for pre-season. “I was sat in Marbella thinking: ‘I want to go back in.’” With the prospect of linking up with Rogers and João Pedro, who has also had a good rest, Palmer has plenty of reasons to be excited.

Off-field picture

July ended with Chelsea being fined £10m and receiving a suspended transfer ban over multiple violations of transfer rules under the ownership of Roman Abramovich. An appeal from the club saved them from a six-point deduction. Chelsea were deemed compliant with the Premier League’s profitability and sustainability rules for the three-year period ending in 2025 despite posting an English record £262.4m pre-tax loss for the 2024-25 season. They have not been cowed by failure to qualify for Europe and have spent over £300m on new signings. For the fourth year in a row, Chelsea look likely to start the season without a front-of-shirt sponsor.

Owner-fan relationship

Supporter protests against the ownership of Todd Boehly’s BlueCo have been a frequent sight on matchdays, including before May’s FA Cup final defeat by Manchester City. There have been reservations about the club’s youth-oriented transfer policy from the start and last season’s failings prompted the co-owner Behdad Eghbali to admit the need “to add more ready-made players” to the squad. Whether fans were expecting the arrivals of Welbeck and Henderson is another question. The introduction of a ticket ballot system for home games has also been unpopular with regular match-going supporters.

The manager

It was a bit of a coup for Chelsea to secure Alonso’s services this summer, especially given the Liverpool job was available. The Spaniard has a reputation to rebuild after his dream job at Real Madrid ended in the sack after six months. “I got a scar, now it is healed,” he said. Alonso’s record of developing young players, such as Florian Wirtz, at Bayer Leverkusen while simultaneously delivering silverware is a match made in heaven for the Chelsea hierarchy. One detail to note: Alonso has been appointed as manager, rather than head coach like his predecessors. He has also brought in Austin MacPhee, Aston Villa’s set-piece guru.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen Chelsea broke the British transfer record to pry Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa. Photograph: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty Images

Chelsea went one better than Manchester City’s £116m signing of Elliot Anderson by bringing in Rogers, who had been linked with Arsenal, for a new British record fee of £117m. Although he started England’s World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina on the right wing, Rogers has thrived for Aston Villa playing largely off the left and should slot in there nicely at Chelsea. The 24-year-old has proved himself in the Premier League and his best-buddy relationship with his former Manchester City youth teammate Palmer is a major plus. “I can see them linking really well,” Alonso said.

Stat attack

Has anyone checked Chelsea haven’t built a squad of Benjamin Buttons? The average age of their starting XI has decreased over the past three seasons when they were already the youngest team in Premier League history. You can see why they signed Henderson and Welbeck.

Set for a breakthrough

Robert Sánchez is still Chelsea’s No 1 but he may face serious competition this season from the 21-year-old Mike Penders. The goalkeeper, who was third-choice for Belgium at the World Cup, was signed from Genk in 2024 and spent last season on loan at Strasbourg in Ligue 1. The comparisons with Thibaut Courtois, who Chelsea signed from Genk at a similar age, are obvious. Like Courtois, Penders is 6ft 7in and therefore has a massive reach, but he also earns plaudits for his passing. Chances will come in cup competitions, but the clamour for Penders to be first choice might become hard to ignore.

World Cup impact

Enzo Fernández had a rollercoaster of a World Cup. Chelsea’s vice-captain popped up with crucial late goals for Argentina in the knockout stages, including a winning header against Egypt and the equaliser against England. But the abiding memory was his part in Argentina’s unsavoury approach in the final against Spain, where he received one yellow card for dissent and another for sending Pau Cubarsí flying. Real Madrid said in July they had “no intention” of pursuing a move that Fernández seemed to covet earlier this year when he said he would “love” to live in Madrid – comments that earned him a two-game ban under Rosenior. How about living in Manchester? City have been linked.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi has ‘quite a few doubts’ about football future after death of his father
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi has hinted that the end of his career may be near after ­admitting to “quite a few doubts” about his football future following the death of his father.

Jorge Messi died last week at the age of 68 in Rosario, Argentina, after a long illness, with his health during this summer’s World Cup appearing to take a toll on Argentina’s 39-year-old captain.

In a tribute on Instagram on Wednesday, Messi wrote: “I don’t know what I’m going to do without you. I don’t know how ​to move forward. I only played football and now I have quite a few doubts about whether I’m going to keep doing it for much longer.

“You were by my side from the beginning; there was so little left until the end. Why couldn’t you hold on just a little longer so we could finish it together?”

Messi ​spent time with his ‌father after the tournament, where Argentina were beaten in the final by Spain, before rejoining his club side, Inter Miami, making his Major League Soccer return against Columbus at the start of this month.

Jorge had been a constant presence during his son’s career from his earliest days at Barcelona, with the World Cup the first time he had been absent from a major tournament. Messi revealed that his father, despite his deteriorating condition, had urged him to play for La Albiceleste in their ultimately unsuccessful attempt to defend their title.

“You always asked me to play in the last World Cup and a few days before it started was when you got worse,” he wrote. “It was the first time you weren’t going to be at a tournament … Every time a match ended, I would ‌wait and hope for your message. That’s when I realised how real the situation was.”

After tearfully celebrating the opening goal of his hat-trick against Algeria in the group stage, Messi had explained he was going through “a few difficult, complicated days” because of “something unrelated to football”. he said he ran out of energy in final.

“My legs couldn’t go on any more,” he wrote. “This time I tried to push myself beyond my ​physical limits, but I couldn’t. ​I never felt well … We weren’t champions, ​but you don’t know how much we enjoyed every match. Once again, you were ​right: I had to ‌be there and play ​it.”

Messi has earned 207 caps for Argentina since making his debut for his country in August 2005. He captained the side to World Cup glory in 2022, matching the achievement of Diego Maradona in 1986, though like Maradona he fell at the final hurdle when attempting to win back-to-back titles.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Messi did, though, break the record for total World Cup goals, with his strike against Egypt in the last 16 his 21st at the tournament and his 125th in all for Argentina. His World Cup tally was later surpassed by France’s Kylian Mbappé in the third-place playoff.

With his future uncertain it remains to be seen whether he will add to his remarkable CV of honours, which includes 10 La Liga titles, four Champions Leagues and eight Ballons d’Or in addition to that World Cup triumph in Qatar.

But he promised to honour his father’s memory through his own children: “I’m going to miss you so much, but you will always be present, especially in the upbringing of my children, because I will teach them and raise them the way you raised me.”

Sports.title: ‘It’s a nice hobby’: Manchester United’s Janina Leitzig on goalkeeping and gardening
Sports.content:
With some parts of England gearing up for a fifth heatwave of 2026 the new Manchester United goalkeeper Janina Leitzig, a keen gardener, is sympathetic to the precarious health of this reporter’s tomato plants. “You’re not used to so little rain, are you?” she observes. For the time being, after her summer move to Manchester, the former Germany youth international does not have a garden of her own but she reveals that, during her three-and-a-half-year spell at her former club Leicester, homegrown vegetables were her pride and joy.

“I love to do some gardening. Back home, everyone has their own vegetables and it’s just better, it tastes better,” she tells the Guardian. “Being away from home and away from family, of course you have your football friends, but still it can be quite lonely sometimes if you come home from training, so it was really nice to have a garden and to spend time outside. It’s not too much effort, it’s just a nice hobby.”

The 27-year-old got her outdoor fix with a spot of surfing in Cornwall this summer during the off-season, but now the serious business of pre-season is well under way. Her new club Manchester United are heading to La Manga for a training camp between 14 and 19 August, where the focus will have to be less on runner beans and more on running drills.

Leitzig, the former Bayern Munich and Hoffenheim keeper, was sitting down for an interview before it was known that the Spanish coach Eva Olid was to become United’s new manager, but explained why swapping Leicester for United was appealing to her. “It’s such a big club and it’s such a big honour to be here,” Leitzig says.

“I think, for every player, it’s really interesting if you have an offer from Manchester United. First of all, the team is so nice. The characters in here – you can tell it’s a really good and strong team. The training quality is really high. The building and the facilities [at Carrington] are really good; it’s really professional here. [When] the conversations were going on [with United], they just gave me a really good feeling.”

View image in fullscreen Janina Leitzig during a training session at Carrington. Photograph: Poppy Townson/MUFC/Getty Images

Leitzig has signed a contract with United until 2029, after the disappointment of relegation with Leicester last season, but says she has nothing but fond feelings about her former club, who she initially joined on loan in January 2023 before signing permanently that summer.

Looking back at what she learned in the East Midlands, she says: “It was such a special time for me. It was supposed to be only half a year and then it ended up being three-and-a-half. I think that says a lot about how much I liked it there. The people are great and the club is great.

“Obviously we had some tough times and unfortunately the relegation last season was really, really tough and it really hurt, because the club deserves to be in a better position, but I really hope that the girls will do well and I see them soon back in the WSL. It would be great if they could come back up quickly.”

During her time in England, Leitzig has observed an evolution in goalkeeping styles, and she is in a thoughtful mood when discussing what the future might look like for keepers, tactically. On the modern trend of keepers playing out from the back, she says: “To be fair, there was one phase where everyone wanted goalkeepers to play with the feet and I think it’s still really important, but I think there was a phase where it was too much. I think it was a bit overexaggerated at times, so I think it’s coming back now to be more about the basic stuff.

“Obviously you have to switch play and you have to be good with your feet under pressure, but I think the game is going to be more [about] trying to get the ball as quick as possible in the opposite half to then keep the pressure up there and not to try to take such a high risk. It’s going to be interesting.

“I think, because I’m German and Manuel Neuer [her idol] is German, I learned quite early to play with both feet and I was an outfield player initially, so I’m feeling confident about playing with the ball. But saving shots is the best part of goalkeeping.”

The USA keeper Phallon Tullis-Joyce played in 21 of United’s 22 matches in the Women’s Super League last season and Leitzig says they will enjoy working together and helping each other. “They [United] said it’s like a competition [to start in goal]. Obviously it’s really important to have strong goalkeepers, because you never know what happens in the season.

“I will just give my best, I’ll try to bring quality, and then it’s the manager’s decision to decide who’s going to play. But it’s really important that we are a good goalkeeper team, that we support each other and push each other because then everyone can get better.”

United, who finished fourth last season, will get the new WSL season under way on the opening night, at London City Lionesses on 4 September. Leizig concludes by looking ahead to that showdown and says, with fire in her eyes: “To have the first game of the season Friday evening, 7pm, floodlights, it’s just something you’re really excited for. Working in the pre-season you think: ‘When can the [games] finally start,’ so I’m really excited for that game.”

Sports.title: Aston Villa boy wonder Brian Madjo can be Harry Kane’s England replacement despite playing for different country three times
Sports.content:
Aston Villa boy wonder Brian Madjo can be Harry Kane’s England replacement despite playing for different country three times

England fans might have been given a glimpse into the future watching Brian Madjo's memorable debut for Aston Villa.

The Villans were beaten 2-1 by Paris Saint-Germain in the UEFA Super Cup, but the Premier League side will be buoyed by the performance of their 17-year-old goalscorer in Salzburg.

4 Madjo took just 45 minutes to open his Aston Villa account Credit: Getty

Desire Doue netted the winning goal for PSG, as he fired the European champions back in front in the 61st minute.

Kvicha Kvaratskhelia had given the French giants an early lead, before Madjo became the main talking point of the first half.

Having signed for Villa for £10 million in January from French club Metz, the teenager was only recently cleared to play after a Court of Arbitration for Sport ruling.

This saw Madjo handed his debut for the Super Cup, and he was immediately in the thick of the action, as he missed a series of glorious chances to equalise.

But his persistence was rewarded on the stroke of half time, as he guided a brilliant close-range volley into the net from John McGinn's cross.

This sparked huge celebrations from the Villa players, as Madjo entered his name into the record books.

At 17 years and 212 days old, the debut goal saw him become the youngest goalscorer in Super Cup history.

And while Madjo has three senior caps for Luxembourg, England fans will be thrilled to discover that he is very much in contention to become a star of the future for the Three Lions.

How can Brian Madjo still play for England?

Born in London, Madjo moved to Luxembourg at a young age, and got his first taste of international football with the European nation.

He represented Luxembourg at Under-15 and Under-16 level before making his senior debut in March 2025.

4 Could England fans be seeing more of Madjo after his standout debut for Aston Villa? Credit: The FA via Getty

And while Madjo has since gone on to take his senior caps tally to three appearances, his international future doesn't appear to lie with Luxembourg.

That is after he opted to switch allegiance to England in September 2025, as he received his first call-up to their Under-17s.

His change in international allegiances is permitted thanks to FIFA's eligibility rules, which have notably seen Declan Rice and Jack Grealish change their national teams.

This allows players who have featured in no more than three competitive matches before turning 21 are able to change nationalities.

But for Madjo, all three of his appearances for Luxembourg came in friendlies against Sweden, Switzerland and Slovenia last year.

This leaves him free to represent his country of birth, in what could now be a hugely encouraging sign for England fans.

4 England will need to consider life after record goalscorer Harry Kane at some point Credit: Getty

With no apparent long-term successor to 33-year-old talisman Harry Kane, Madjo could stake his claim as he looks to lead the line for Villa this season.

The teenager showcased huge physical pressure for a teenager against PSG, as well as taking up goalscoring positions.

His debut goal in the Super Cup saw him follow up on his impressive pre-season debut against Walsall, where he netted twice in a 5-0 win.

His prowess has long been known in Luxembourg, where he first made a name for himself in the Racing Union.

So much so in fact, that the club's academy director Delvin Skenderovic recently told talkSPORT.com: "I think he reminds me a lot of Romelu Lukaku.

"I think he has quite a similar profile where he's able to keep the ball, he's strong with his head.

4 Lukaku has been named in both the Serie A and Premier League teams of the year Credit: Getty

"But I just think Brian will be a little bit faster than Lukaku."

Sports.title: Myles Lewis-Skelly keeps fans guessing with Arsenal goal celebration as Mikel Arteta responds to question on transfer speculation
Sports.content:
Myles Lewis-Skelly keeps fans guessing with Arsenal goal celebration as Mikel Arteta responds to question on transfer speculation

Mikel Arteta says Myles Lewis-Skelly being linked with other clubs is a 'good sign' after the Arsenal star's cryptic celebration on Wednesday night.

Lewis-Skelly appeared to send a message to Arsenal fans after his goal during a pre-season friendly at home to Como.

2 Lewis-Skelly appeared to send a message to Arsenal fans after scoring against Como Credit: Getty

It came a day after talkSPORT revealed the versatile youngster had been offered to multiple Premier League clubs by the Gunners.

The 19-year-old found the target against Como at the Emirates Stadium on Wednesday night to open the scoring in the first half.

Como later equalised through Martin Baturina before half-time as the match ended 1-1.

Arsenal message?

Although Arsenal went on to win 4-3 on penalties, it was Lewis-Skelly's goal celebration which caught the attention of the fans.

The teenager gestured to the home fans before being congratulated by his teammates.

Footage captured from the stands appeared to show him apologising as he held up his hands before making a heart gesture.

Lewis-Skelly also tapped the Arsenal badge on his shirt before walking back towards his own half.

His reaction to scoring follows rising speculation over a potential exit from the Premier League champions.

One fan asked: "Is he saying bye?"

Another added: "Myles Lewis-Skelly celebrates by apologising to the Arsenal fans before throwing up a heart with his hands. One of our own, forever."

While this decisive fan declared: "He is going nowhere."

Arteta addresses Lewis-Skelly reports

Despite being encouraged by his player being in demand, Arteta refused to divulge any details on where the player could end up before deadline day on September 1.

“He’s a very emotional player. Remember when he did all the gestures on the pitch. I am not going to talk about any speculation," Arteta said.

“If there is any speculation about our players it is a good sign, it means we attract attention and they are doing a good job.”

Lewis-Skelly's future

The England international, who can feature at both left-back and in midfield has been offered to clubs ahead of the transfer window closing.

Amongst those sides are top-flight rivals Manchester United and Chelsea. Clubs had already been made aware of Lewis-Skelly's availability earlier in the summer.

However, fresh contact was made following Arsenal's signing of Bruno Guimaraes. The Brazil midfielder joined the club from Newcastle United for £75million on Saturday.

Lewis-Skelly has four years remaining on his current deal in north London after signing a new contract last summer.

2 Chelsea and United are amongst the clubs Lewis-Skelly has been offered to Credit: Getty

Having graduated from Arsenal's famed Hale End academy, he has already made 75 appearances for the club.

Of those, 20 came in the Premier League last season as the Gunners won their first title for 22 years.

Having played 62 minutes from the start against Como, Lewis-Skelly will hope to feature in Sunday's Community Shield.

Arsenal face Manchester City in the season's traditional curtain-raiser at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff on Sunday.

Lewis-Skelly has started all four of his side's pre-season fixtures so far this summer.

As well as his goal against Como, he also provided an assist for Max Dowman in a 4-1 win over Girona earlier month.

Sports.title: Cristian Romero takes big step towards Atletico Madrid transfer despite Tottenham agreeing fee with Serie A club
Sports.content:
Atletico Madrid have agreed a deal in principle to sign Cristian Romero for a fee worth £34million, talkSPORT understands.

The Tottenham captain has long been tipped for a summer exit from north London, and Spurs had already agreed a fee with Napoli for the defender.



5 Romero's time at Spurs looks to be up Credit: Getty

The Serie A club were set to pay £34m for Romero, but were unable to agree terms with the player.

More recently, Romero was linked with a shock switch to Spurs' bitter rivals Arsenal, but any chance of this now looks to have ended.

Inter Milan also held talks earlier with him in the summer, but the Argentine is now set to get his dream move to Spain.



With a fee now agreed for him to join Atletico, Spurs will also retain a 15 per cent sell-on clause on any future transfer.

This comes after Romero agreed personal terms with LaLiga giants Atletico with the player to sign a four-year deal which has the option of a further year.



Romero is now set to join up with compatriot Diego Simeone at Atletico, in a move that will bring to an end his five-year stay at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

His expected £34m move also means that Spurs will make a loss on the £43million they paid Atalanta to sign Romero in 2021.



Tottenham's defensive overhaul

Spurs have signed centre-backs Jan Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi this summer, with Micky van de Ven in positive talks over a new five-year deal.

This left Romero free to leave the club, despite penning a contract extension through to 2029 last August.

His imminent exit comes after he drew criticism from fans for his conduct and ill-discipline last season.

5 Romero now looks set to join Diego Simeone and his Argentine contingent at Atletico Madrid



Romero was sent off twice in 23 league appearances, and received ten yellow cards as Spurs narrowly avoided relegation.

The 2022 World Cup winner also became embroiled in a storm in May when it was reported that he was to miss Tottenham's crucial final game of the season in favour of a return to his homeland to watch formative club Belgrano.

With Spurs at risk of relegation and Romero getting wind of fan disgruntlement, he later changed his mind and instead was on hand to support his teammates in their quest for survival.

'Get rid of him'

As Romero closes in on a move away from north London, talkSPORT's Jamie O'Hara had no qualms about Tottenham losing their captain.



Discussing the defender's links with Arsenal last week, the Sport Bar host and former Spurs player insisted the club would be better off without him, and claimed their new arrivals are better options.

Speaking on talkSPORT Breakfast, O'Hara said: “Get rid of him. I've heard there’s Arsenal chat about him - get rid of him.

5 The Argentine seeing red became a frustratingly familiar sight for Spurs fans in recent seasons Credit: Getty

“He was a liability for us last season. We’ve finished 17th in the last two seasons - he was the captain. He didn't want to be there on the last day. It was only because he got told that he had to come back that he ended up coming back.



“So get rid of him. We've got better players now. He's a liability.

“Van de Ven - make him captain. He's a player that you want in your side. You got Senesi, Van Hecke. Romero isn't even going to play.”

After two disappointing league campaigns, Tottenham have set about kickstarting a new era under Roberto De Zerbi this summer.

Spurs have splashed the cash in a bid to rebuild, spending £237m in total which includes twice breaking their club transfer record - first to sign Mateus Fernandes and then Sandro Tonali from West Ham and Newcastle respectively.

And O'Hara insisted there is no place for Romero in De Zerbi's new-look team, even after playing a central role in Argentina's run to the World Cup final.



5 Van Hecke looks set to fill Romero's boots after his £52million arrival from Brighton Credit: Getty

5 Romero helped Argentina through to a second consecutive World Cup final this summer, but his best form has often eluded him at Spurs Credit: Getty

Continuing to blast Romero, he added: “I'm happy to see the back of him.

"We need a new era under De Zerbi and it looks like he's putting a right good team together. We'll see what happens, but it looks like we've got a right good team and the players seem to like him.



“But Romero isn’t part of it. Get rid of him, get as much as we can."

Sports.title: Referee ends Manchester United vs Leeds friendly early
Sports.content:
Normal time of Manchester United's friendly against Leeds United was ended early after a string of pitch invaders disrupted the match.

The pre-season clash at Croke Park in Dublin was the first ever club football match at the iconic venue but was marred right at the end when multiple fans ran onto the pitch.

3 United's clash with Leeds was ended early after a pitch invasion by six supporters Credit: Getty

As the clock ticked down towards the 90th minute, a young supporter cleared the advertising hoardings.

Play was immediately stopped before five more fans invaded the pitch to take selfies with the players.

Whilst the TV cameras panned away from the incident, cheers could be heard from the crowd as each supporter entered the field.

Due to the disruption, referee Neil Doyle blew the final whistle before play restarted, without any added time indicated.

Meanwhile, it was announced on the PA system inside the stadium threatening to stop the match again if there were any more pitch invasions.

With the score level at 1-1, a penalty shootout followed once the pitch invaders had been removed.

United win on penalties

And the bragging rights belonged to Man United as they emerged victorious in the shootout, winning 5-4.

The decisive moment saw Noussair Mazraoui score the winning penalty after James Justin struck the crossbar with his effort.

United had appeared in control of the shootout after summer signing Harry Wilson was denied for Leeds by Dermot Mee.

However, an uncharacteristic miss from Bruno Fernandes as he sent his spot-kick wide resulted in sudden death efforts.

3 United beat Leeds on penalties to win the BOYLE Sports Cup Credit: Getty

The Red Devils captain's blushes were spared, though, after Youri Tielemans and Mazraoui found the target.

In doing so, United also get their hands on a piece of silverware by lifting the BOYLE Sports Cup.

Joshua Zirkzee had opened the scoring during the first half in the Irish capital.

His 16th minute strike made history as the first-ever club goal scored at Croke Park in its 142-year existence.

The match was the first association football match of any kind played at the 82,300-capacity stadium for 17 years.

Zirkzee's goal was cancelled out before half-time as Brenden Aaronson levelled for Leeds.

3 Zirkzee scored the first-ever club football goal at Croke Park Credit: Getty

When do United and Leeds play next?

United will now conclude their pre-season schedule against AC Milan on Saturday.

The two sides meet at the Wroclaw Stadium in Poland this weekend.

Michael Carrick's side then begin their Premier League campaign away to newly-promoted Hull City on August 22.

As for Leeds, they host Augsburg at Elland Road on Saturday before visiting Nottingham Forest on the opening weekend of the season.

Sports.title: Jeff Stelling predicts 2026/27 Premier League table and tips shock side for relegation
Sports.content:
Jeff Stelling has made his predictions for the 2026/27 Premier League season, including a surprise tip for relegation.

The new campaign gets underway next Friday (August 21) with champions Arsenal hosting newly promoted Coventry.



2 Mikel Arteta's Arsenal will be aiming to retain their Premier League title Credit: Getty

That's the first of 380 top-flight games to be played between then and May, with plenty of twists and turns inevitable.

But Stelling has already put his neck on the line by naming his picks for the title, European qualification and the drop.

Predicting the full Premier League table on talkSPORT, Stelling backed Arsenal to retain their title with Chelsea as runners-up, followed by Manchester City in third and Manchester United in fourth.



He placed Tottenham fifth – which has been enough for Champions League qualification in each of the last two campaigns – and Liverpool sixth, with Newcastle seventh and Aston Villa eighth.

Fulham to fall?

However, perhaps Stelling's most eye-catching prediction came at the bottom end of the table, where he felt Fulham would go down.



Joining Stelling on air, Peterborough chairman Darragh MacAnthony and former Villa striker Gabby Agbonlahor voiced their conerns over Fulham.

As well as Alvaro Arbeloa replacing Marco Silva as head coach, the Cottagers have lost key players this summer such as Harry Wilson and Raul Jimenez.



Between them, Wilson and Jimenez accounted for more than a third of Fulham's Premier League goals last term.

"We called it as well, like two weeks, three weeks ago, didn't we, about Fulham," noted Agbonlahor. "We agreed that that's our team that could be under pressure..."

Stelling believes that Fulham could be in "big, big trouble" in the upcoming campaign.

2 Arbeloa is one of nine new Premier League managers for the start of the 2026/27 season Credit: Getty



The Cottagers' ostensible replacements for Wilson and Jimenez are youngsters Cesar Palacios and Gonzalo Garcia, both of whom have followed Arbeloa from Real Madrid.

And while striker Garcia scored six LaLiga goals at an average of just over one every 30 minutes last season, it remains to be seen how he'll fare in the more testing environment of the Premier League.

Fulham face a tough-looking opening fixture when they host West London rivals Chelsea on Monday, August 24.

Stelling positive about Sky Blues

While he tipped Fulham to be relegated alongside newly promoted Ipswich and Hull, Stelling joined MacAnthony in backing last term's Championship winners Coventry to survive – putting them 15th in his table.



Justifying his decision, he said: "Coventry...spent a lot of money – not on a huge number of players actually. They've chosen quality over quantity.

"Scored a lot of set-plays last season and that could be big for them again this season."

Jeff Stelling's full predicted 2026/27 Premier League table

Sports.title: Roberto Martinez snubbed for Netherlands manager job with World Cup winner appointed
Sports.content:
Xavi has officially been announced as the new head coach of the Netherlands national team.

Roberto Martinez had looked the favourite to take the reins of the Dutch national team, who had been without a manager following Ronald Koeman's departure.



4 Xavi is making his return to the dugout Credit: Getty

Having stepped down as Portugal boss after their World Cup exit, Martinez was free to make an immediate return to management.

However, though the 53-year-old was interviewed for the Netherlands vacancy, he was ultimately turned down.

And in the Spaniard's place, the Netherlands have now appointed footballing legend and former Barcelona manager, Xavi.



The 46-year-old has not managed since his departure from the Camp Nou in 2024, where he spent three years in charge of his former club.

He guided Barca to LaLiga glory in the 2022/23 campaign, before leaving his role after a trophyless 2023/24 season.



As a player, Xavi played a key role in Spain's World Cup triumph in 2010, where they beat the Netherlands 1-0 in the final in Johannesburg, South Africa.

Before his three years as Barcelona boss, the legendary midfielder began his managerial career at Qatari team Al Sadd.



He spent 18 months in charge of the Middle Eastern outfit, winning seven trophies during this time.

'A great honour'

With Xavi the new Netherlands boss, he has become the first foreign manager of their national team in 48 years, after the Austrian Ernst Happel held the role between 1977 and 1978.

Reacting to his appointment, the Spain icon said: “It is a great honour to become head coach of the Netherlands national team.

4 Xavi enjoyed the greatest night of his international career against the Netherlands in 2010 Credit: Getty



4 Martinez stood down from his role as Portugal boss in the aftermath of their World Cup exit Credit: Getty

"As someone who was developed at the FC Barcelona academy, with strong influences from, among others, Johan Cruyff and Rinus Michels, I feel a special connection to Dutch football.

"You could say I am, in a way, a son of Dutch football. Other great coaches, especially Louis van Gaal, under whom I made my debut at Barcelona, and Frank Rijkaard, have also played an important role in shaping me as both a player and as a coach.”

“The Netherlands has a rich football culture and a clear vision that strongly appeals to me: attacking football, based on possession, with creativity, passion and conviction.
