“Of course, the main objective is always to win, but I prefer to do so in a way that reflects those characteristics and that people can enjoy watching.

"The potential is there, as well as a strong foundation to build on.

"I am looking forward to starting this challenge together with the players, the staff and everyone within the KNVB.”

4 Koeman recently stepped down after his second spell in charge of the Dutch national team Credit: Getty

Twist in the tale

Martinez had looked primed to take the Netherlands job, when reports in Holland claimed he was being lined up to succeed Koeman.



However, despite being interviewed for the role, with Dutch media revealing he spoke to he held talks with KNVB technical director Nigel de Jong over the position, his time away from international management will now continue.

The ex-Premier League manager spent six-and-a-half-years with Belgium, before his appointment as Portugal boss in 2023.

Despite his contract expiring at the end of July, Martinez immediately left his role after Portugal lost 1-0 to Spain in the last-16.

He was one of 17 managers that left their position as head coach either during the global tournament in North America, or after their run in the competition concluded.



The Netherlands were among those countries, with former boss Koeman calling time on his three-and-a-half-year spell in charge after Holland lost to Morocco on penalties in the round of 32 stage.

Martinez was among a number of high-profile names to miss out on the role, with Dutch publication De Telegraaf also reporting that Arne Slot, Erik ten Hag and Peter Bosz have passed up on the chance to take the reigns.

Sports.title: Wrexham sell defender to Championship rival
Sports.content:
Wrexham defender Lewis Brunt has completed a permanent move to Bolton Wanderers.

The centre-back has joined the newly-promoted Championship side on a four-year deal.

3 Brunt has joined Bolton from Wrexham on a four-year deal Credit: AFP

Brunt departs the Racecourse Ground after two seasons with the Red Dragons.

The 25-year-old was part of the side which won promotion from League One in 2024/25 following his arrival from Leicester City.

He is now set to face Wrexham in the second-tier this season as a result of joining the Trotters.

Brunt made 41 appearances for his former club, including nine in the Championship last term, scoring once.

Wrexham finished their first campaign at the level for 43 years in seventh place, missing out on the play-offs by two points.

They have since completed the permanent signings of goalkeeper Anthony Patterson, Crystal Palace full-back Danny Imray and former Preston North End captain Ben Whiteman ahead of the new season.

Brunt joins Bolton

Meanwhile, Bolton were promoted via the League One play-offs, ending their seven-year absence from the Championship.

Brunt becomes the club's eighth summer signing and their second from Wrexham.

He follows striker Ryan Hardie, who has arrived at the Toughsheet Community Stadium on a season-long loan.

Bolton have also added Luca Stephenson, Akin Famewo, Kyliane Dong, Gaizka Larrazabal, David Watson and Ben Davies to their ranks.

3 Brunt made 41 appearances for Wrexham and was part of their League One promotion-winning side Credit: PA

Speaking to the club's website, Brunt explained: "Stepping up from League One to the Championship is a big step up but if I can come into the building and try and help the lads and help the team then that's what I'll do.

"It’s going to be a challenge but it's one I'm sure the group, the staff, the team are all looking forward to and hopefully we can make it a positive season."

Bolton debut

Brunt was not involved in Wrexham's Carabao Cup defeat to Middlesbrough last Friday having been left out of the matchday squad.

He could now make his Bolton debut as early as this weekend with Steven Schumacher's side returning to league action at home to Lancashire rivals Preston on Saturday. The match is scheduled to kick-off at 12.30pm, live on talkSPORT.

Brunt will have to wait until December 11 to face his former club, though, as Wrexham make the trip to Bolton.

The two sides then meet in north Wales for the reverse fixture on New Year's Day.

Sports.title: Chelsea send Enzo Fernandez transfer ultimatum as Blues urged to keep £120m ‘dirty winner’
Sports.content:
Chelsea have set a deadline of 5pm this Friday for Manchester City to complete a deal for Enzo Fernandez, takSPORT understands.

The 25-year-old currently faces an uncertain future in west London, after he previously fuelled rumours of his exit, with the Citizens said to be keen on him poaching from their Premier League rivals.

4 Fernandez faces an uncertain future at Stamford Bridge Credit: Getty

Fernandez heavily hinted at a move to Real Madrid towards the end of last season, only for the Spanish giants to shut this down in a statement saying they have 'no intention' of signing him.

A move to the Etihad could be appealing for the Argentine, which would offer him a reunion with former Blues boss Enzo Maresca.

Maresca left left Stamford Bridge on New Year's Day after a breakdown in relations at the club, a decision which Fernandez later appeared to criticise the Chelsea board over.

But with Fernandez boasting a huge £120million price tag, talkSPORT's Ben Jacobs recently revealed City could be deterred by this.

And they have now been handed an ultimatum, as Jacobs confirmed the Sky Blues have been told they until Friday to complete a deal.

Maresca's side are said to be keen on Argentina star, while Chelsea have made it clear his £120m asking price will only stay until Friday.

Following his involvement in the 2026 World Cup, where he helped Argentina to the final, Fernandez has since returned to Chelsea for pre-season training.

Chelsea told to keep Fernandez

The latest on Fernandez's future comes after former Manchester United goalkeeper Ben Foster urged Chelsea to do their utmost to keep him, calling him the 'dirty winner' that they need.

New Blues boss Xabi Alonso has previously voiced his desire to keep Fernandez, but his public comments hinting at a departure have understandably seen a number of fans turn against him.

His public image wasn't done any favours during the World Cup, when he drew the ire of England fans by mocking the Three Lions with a social media post playing their unofficial 'Wonderwall' anthem after Argentina's semi-final victory.

4 Fernandez made a pointed celebration after scoring against England in the World Cup semi-finals Credit: Getty

Despite Fernandez dividing opinion, former England stopper Foster has urged Chelsea to look past this and do their utmost to keep him.

With the midfielder playing a crucial role in Argentina's 2022 World Cup glory, Foster insisted he has the nasty streak needed to inspire a team to success.

Asked if he felt Chelsea would fare well without him on Tuesday's talkSPORT, the former goalkeeper said: “I still think they need to keep him. He's a little ferret, is what he is.

“But he's a winner. He's a horrible, dirty little winner that you want in your team. It's as simple as that."

Co-host Shebahn Aherne agreed that Fernandez's behaviour has long been divisive, pointing to his conduct at the World Cup.

The Blues star was sent off in Argentina's final defeat to Spain, as he received two yellow cards in quick succession, the second of which saw him send Pau Cubarsi flying into the air.

4 Xabi Alonso would benefit from having Fernandez among his midfield options, insists Foster Credit: Getty

Aherne said: “He was a disgrace. But listen, we've seen that with him before. We've seen his behaviour like that the whole time."

But Foster then insisted: “You want it in your team though.”

Fernandez has proven he brings more than just steely ruthlessness to a team during his time at Stamford Bridge.

Since joining Chelsea in January 2023 for a then British transfer record fee of £106m, the Argentina international has shown his ability to score goals from midfield, netting ten times in the Premier League last term.

End game for Fernandez?

While Foster insisted Fernandez' ruthless streak is what Chelsea need, it remains to be seen if the club will take the same view.

And while City have now been given a hard deadline over a deal for the World Cup winner, Jacobs recently revealed City could stop short of another nine-digit transfer.

4 Maresca and Fernandez shared a close bond while at Chelsea Credit: Getty

The Citizens have so far signed Elliot Anderson for £116m, while they are now in advanced talks with Lille over Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi, for a fee expected to be in the region of £100m.

On Fernandez, Jacobs told talkSPORT earlier this week: "Chelsea's asking price was £120million. Now, maybe that's higher if you consider the fact that other deals, like Elliot Anderson - £116million.

"And Chelsea may argue that Enzo Fernandez should be more. He's a World Cup winner after all, and he was the vice-captain and captain at times of Chelsea.

“So Chelsea are calm about the situation, and they have every intent, if the window shuts, to try and get Enzo Fernandez on one extreme to sign the new deal.

“And yet, if their valuation is met, an exit is possible.

“We know that Enzo Fernandez has flirted with a move to Real Madrid. But if we take the public statement at face value, even with Rodri heading to Barcelona, the expectation is that Real won't move. You can never say never with Real, but they were put off by that asking price, according to my information.”

“So yes, City - specifically Enzo Maresca - do appreciate Enzo Fernandez. Are they going to find that budget questionable?

Sports.title: Why the alarm bells should be ringing at Newcastle after defeat by Everton: Squad's lack of depth exposed, the key man who looks out of sorts and midfield puzzle new boss Matthias Jaissle must solve, writes CRAIG HOPE
Sports.content:
In their new change kit, Newcastle United were the ‘shrinking violets’ during a 3-1 defeat by Everton at Murrayfield.

The loss raises serious questions over the squad’s readiness for the Premier League season, with new boss Matthias Jaissle having inherited a group lacking leadership as well as quality in key areas.

David Moyes’ side were the deserved winners after goals from Thierno Barry, Iliman Ndiaye and Tyrique George settled a contest in which the Toffees showed more control and composure. Harvey Barnes fired a late reply for the Magpies.

Here, our chief footballer reporter Craig Hope brings you his four big takeaways for Newcastle to consider…

NEW FACES NEEDED

This was not a ‘reality check’ for Newcastle, because the reality of their situation was already blindingly obvious. They have lost four of their best and most experienced players this summer and head coach Eddie Howe said he could not continue on the eve of pre-season.

Here, it was not just holes in Newcastle’s XI that were exposed, but the depth of their squad looks alarmingly shallow. They need two full-backs, better midfielders and a fresh spark in attack. The danger for Jaissle is that he makes a losing start because he has been left short.

New boss Matthias Jaissle has plenty to think about but the problems were not unexpected

We understand that Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba is among those the manager admires, and the club have him on their list of targets. It is not an active transfer – the 22-year-old currently has an ankle injury – but our sources say it is one to keep an eye on as the window progresses.

Baleba would be an ambitious move, but Newcastle need to be just that if they are to give their new boss a squad that is able to compete in the top-flight this term. For right now, you would forecast a season-long struggle at the wrong end of the table.

On transfers, Jaissle said: ‘I think you all see the matches. You're also smart enough to see the needs in the squad. We handle these things internally. We are aware of what we need. There's still some time.’

He added: ‘For sure, we cannot be on the peak (against Liverpool on the opening day). This is clear. We're just working now for a couple of days.’

SVEN LOOKS SHORT

Sven Botman signed a new four-year contract in January but his performances since have been below the level that earned him that deal. Insiders were concerned that he looked too rigid in his movement towards the end of the season, and that worry has extended into the summer.

The Dutch centre-back is a class act at his best, but he was again at fault for a goal here and his sloppiness on the ball perhaps betrays a lack of confidence. After a series of injuries, the wider concern would be that his best days are behind him. He has a lot to prove this season. For now, Dan Burn would appear a better bet at left-sided centre-back alongside Malick Thiaw.

Sven Botman looked a little off the pace at Murrayfield as Everton outclassed Newcastle

MIDFIELD RIDDLE

For five years under Howe, Newcastle have played with a midfield three. Jaissle, in his first two games, has started with a 4-2-3-1, and an absence of control was all too evident during the first-half period in which Everton scored twice.

Joelinton and new signing Aladji Bamba were the pair in the middle, but the former has always preferred the insurance of two team-mates alongside him, allowing him to charge around and impose his physical superiority.

He is not suited to a more disciplined role in which he needs to take better care of the ball, while Bamba, 20, clearly needs time before he is ready to start in the Premier League. The Frenchman, formerly of Monaco, has made only 25 senior appearances in his career.

If Newcastle going into the season opener against Liverpool with this midfield, you suspect it would not end well.

Harvey Barnes scored a consolation goal for the Geordies, giving their fans something to cheer

STEUR THE POSITIVE (AGAIN)

On a positive note, Jacob Ramsey and Sean Steur were a better combination in the second half. Steur, 18, has been Newcastle’s best player during pre-season and he again showed a maturity beyond his teenage years. His willingness to take the ball in tight areas – and then keep it – is exactly what this team needs in a world without Bruno Guimaraes.

Steur apart, however, ball retention is going to be a problem for Newcastle. And when they have a defence that looks short of pace, the opposition springing quick breaks on the back of turnovers should be a worry for Jaissle.

Sports.title: Arsenal's next top prospect shines in absence of key man, Myles Lewis-Skelly makes his case after doubts over his future - and why time is running out for Gabriel Jesus
Sports.content:
Arsenal's next top prospect shines in absence of key man, Myles Lewis-Skelly makes his case after doubts over his future - and why time is running out for Gabriel Jesus

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Myles Lewis-Skelly struck in the first half in Arsenal’s 1-1 draw against Cesc Fabregas’ Como side amid speculation around his future.

Lewis-Skelly's effort was cancelled out by Martin Baturina two minutes before the break in what proved to be a real test for Mikel Arteta's men.

The Gunners went on to win 4-3 on penalties, thanks largely to David Raya. Arsenal are back in action when they face Manchester City in the Community Shield on Sunday.

Daily Mail Sport's ISAAN KHAN brings you the main talking points from their win over the Italian side.

Marli Salmon stands out

There’s another young gem coming through Arsenal’s Hale End pipeline: enter Marli Salmon.

He stepped up on a night where Mikel Arteta threw down the challenge to his youngsters.

Salmon and Max Dowman, both 16, started, as well as Theo Julienne, 18, who made his first senior team start.

Salmon in particular stood out, for the rarity of a 16-year-old starting in a first-team match at centre back.

The defender last season would typically come on at right back when substituted on in the odd first-team game — once in the Champions League and three times in the FA Cup (he started against Mansfield Town).

Marli Salmon was given a warm embrace from his manager Mikel Arteta when he came off

He coped well and wasn’t deterred by the physical challenge, playing with steel and conviction.

The opposition were wary of taking Salmon on, with the menacing Gabriel alongside him.

His runs and confidence on the ball made the real mark, as he progressed into the opposition half on occasion, evading players with a burst of speed. That takes guts and took the crowd by surprise.

What a baptism of fire such an experience is, and one he will no doubt remember.

Arteta’s confidence in the teenager saw Salmon stay on the pitch until the 88th minute.

He stepped up, alright.

Lewis-Skelly makes his point

A heart-shaped celebration and hands folded in a prayer motion, Myles Lewis-Skelly made his point.

The teenager struck in the first half amid reports suggesting the 19-year-old has been offered to Chelsea and Manchester United by intermediaries, which Arsenal have insisted isn’t the case.

Though Lewis-Skelly brushed the noise aside to enjoy a promising display in a young line-up.

Goalkeeper Jean Butez’s clearance was headed down by Lewis-Skelly to Gabriel Martinelli, who teed up the teenager to strike home on 33 minutes.

The goal was met by chants of ‘Myles Lewis-Skelly, he’s one of our own’, on an evening he used to remind observers of his talents.

Myles Lewis-Skelly delivered a clear message with his celebration amid talk over his future

Yet, it was the midfielder’s actions after the goal which reflected where his intentions lie.

Lewis-Skelly clasped his hands together towards the crowd before making out a heart sign in a clear sign of intent.

He is a fine player, and one who started in last season’s Champions League final.

His ceiling is high — and his future is bright at Arsenal.

Little chance of resurrection for Jesus

The gauntlet had been laid. With Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz on the bench, Gabriel Jesus started as the No 9.

It represented a nudge from Arteta, as if to say ‘show me what you’ve got’.

That didn’t last long, hooked off on 32 minutes for Gyokeres after a limited cameo.

He did try, the Brazilian. The effort was there, trying to pierce the backline with darts forward and active around the goal.

Gabriel Jesus' future looks in doubt and he made way for Viktor Gyokeres

Though his display was marked by a miss on six minutes, the ball falling to him as Eberechi Eze passed on Ethan Nwaneri’s interception.

Jesus had an open goal to aim at with the goalkeeper out of his area — but struck the goalframe.

It dented the forward’s confidence, and he never properly recovered. On 32 minutes, he made way for Gyokeres, a reflection of his underwhelming night.

With just one more friendly remaining — against Manchester City in the Community Shield on Sunday — time is really running out for the Brazilian, who has been earmarked for the door.

Arteta gets one over ex-Gunners star

From afar, the touchline resemblance of Arteta and Cesc Fabregas was uncanny.

Arms crossed, wearing beige trousers and dark-coloured short-sleeved tops, both men mirrored one another.

The pair played alongside each other at Arsenal once upon a time. And at one stage, rumours suggested Fabregas could one day be Arteta’s successor.

Cesc Fabregas was looking dapper back at the Emirates on the touchline

Though such a prospect is a long way off after Arsenal’s title triumph last season.

Still, Fabregas’ post-match press conference lasted over 10 minutes, with Arteta waiting outside for him to finish.

He clearly had missed the Emirates.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick offers clear indication Marcus Rashford will STAY at Man United: Star in manager's plans as forward prepares for return to action against the man who exiled him
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick offers clear indication Marcus Rashford will STAY at Man United: Star in manager's plans as forward prepares for return to action against the man who exiled him

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Marcus Rashford could make his first appearance since returning to Manchester United against AC Milan on Saturday – managed by Ruben Amorim, the man who bombed him out in the first place.

The England international has returned from a loan spell at Barcelona and is now intent on fighting to regain his place at Old Trafford.

He has been told he’s in Michael Carrick’s plans after United’s draw with Leeds in Dublin. By a quirk of fate, it is against Amorim’s Milan side that he will make his return, after an extended post-World Cup break.

Bryan Mbeumo led the line again here and got the assist for Joshua Zirkzee’s goal, but Carrick said of Rashford: ‘He’s our player. He’s come back great. He’s just like any other player... He gives us something a little bit different.’

The summer has been as much about evolution as it has been revolution, with the results of the Mbeumo striker experiment yielding some fascinating results.

The Cameroon international, 27, is far from your typical No9 but for Carrick, that is a big part of his appeal.

Marcus Rashford is in Michael Carrick's plans after his return to Manchester United

United want to give academy star Shea Lacey some space in the first team and he predominantly plays off the right. There is also Amad Diallo, who is facing a defining season in that right-side role. Then you must add in the fact United only have one orthodox No9 option, Benjamin Sesko, and he hasn’t kicked a ball during pre-season due to a shin injury – although he did travel to Ireland to take part in this week-long training camp. Rashford could nudge himself ahead of the Slovenian.

Mbeumo as a striker, and a fluid one at that, holds great appeal and perhaps importance, especially if United do not sign another striker before the September 1 transfer deadline.

Mbeumo’s goals dried up in the second-half of last season and he struggled to rediscover the momentum that had United fans off their seats in the first-half of the campaign.

It led to questions over how Carrick could get the best out of him. But his double against Atletico Madrid in Stockholm, the equaliser in Gothenburg against Paris Saint-Germain and a brilliant piece of skill, coupled with an assist, for Zirkzee to open the scoring here against Leeds in Dublin showed just how much confidence is running through Mbeumo’s veins.

For the opening goal – and he should have had one of his own in the first half when he crashed a shot against the crossbar – he nutmegged two Leeds players as he burst down the left before playing Zirkzee through to score beyond new No1 James Trafford.

Leeds went on to equalise through Brenden Aaronson in the first half and were good value for it after a rocky start.

Despite Carrick’s side dominating the ball when their main men came on, it finished 1-1 in front of an 82,000-strong sell-out crowd at Croke Park. United won 5-4 on penalties.

Mbeumo is set to start as a centre forward at Hull City to kick-start United’s Premier League campaign on August 22. From there the sky feels like the limit for him. This is a formula now, not just an experiment.

Sports.title: PSG 2-1 Aston Villa: French giants claim UEFA Super Cup triumph but two teen stars show future is bright for Villans - with 17-year-old Brian Madjo bullying Luis Enrique's defence
Sports.content:
PSG 2-1 Aston Villa: French giants claim UEFA Super Cup triumph but two teen stars show future is bright for Villans - with 17-year-old Brian Madjo bullying Luis Enrique's defence

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The UEFA Super Cup belongs to Paris Saint-Germain but Aston Villa left Salzburg with something far more precious than a piece of pre-season silverware.

Between them, teenagers Brian Madjo and George Hemmings have made just six competitive appearances for Villa. Yet both frightened the life out of the back-to-back Champions League winners and on this evidence, they will be given plenty more opportunities by Unai Emery.

They may have sold £150million worth of talent in Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne since winning the Europa League and have doubts over the future of other key players. There is nothing quite like teenagers stepping up to the mark, though, and their performances will give Villa plenty of encouragement ahead of their Premier League opener at Brighton on August 23.

Madjo, 17, became the youngest scorer in Super Cup history when he steered home John McGinn’s cross just before half-time. Before that, the 6ft 4ins centre-forward missed two other excellent chances and bullied Willian Pacho, one of the world’s best centre-backs.

Villa signed Madjo for £10m from Metz last January but a registration issue meant he was not cleared to play until this summer.

‘Having days like today is very important for them,’ said Emery. ‘They show how are they are learning after their hard work. This is the way, we decided before the game how we wanted to play this game, we have worked the players in these positions. They showed they are close to playing and competing regularly with us.’

Achraf Hakimi lifts the UEFA Super Cup for PSG after their 2-1 win over Aston Villa

Desire Doue beat the offside trap to put PSG 2-1 up against Aston Villa in Salzburg

English 17-year-old Brian Madjo had a number of chances and converted the equaliser

Either side of Madjo’s strike, goals from Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue ensured PSG retained this trophy, and it is important to say PSG were some way from full fitness.

Yet many of Villa’s players were not in peak condition, either. Luckily, Hemmings was one of those determined to make his mark.

The 19-year-old is a product of Villa’s youth system and given the club’s struggles with UEFA’s financial rules, a homegrown player in the first team is a gem. Though Madjo caught the eye for his goal and chances, Hemmings looks the more accomplished player at this stage.

Starting on the left, he was prepared to run fearlessly at Achraf Hakimi, probably the best right-back on the planet. He showed great maturity in possession, too, at once stage winning the ball from Nuno Mendes close to his own-goal line and casually chipping it to Emi Buendia. Expect to see plenty more of this kid in the weeks ahead.

Now Emery’s attention must turn to the market, where he has been fallible during his time at Villa Park. Despite Madjo’s display, another forward will surely arrive while Villa continue to make progress in deals for midfielder Joao Palhinha and left-back Matteo Ruggeri.

Villa have changed a great deal since they won the Europa League less than three months ago. Gone are Rogers and Tielemans, two of their scorers against Freiburg that night, while Digne was sitting on the PSG bench. Three of Emery’s coaching team have also moved on.

That meant only five of the starters in Istanbul featured here, with Ezri Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emi Martinez still on their post-World Cup breaks. With Arsenal offering a £45million package for Konsa earlier in the day, it is unclear how many more times the England centre-back will wear Villa colours.

Emery and skipper John McGinn were bullish about the ‘new Villa’ on Tuesday and in the first half against PSG, we saw why. Though the majority of the PSG group are some way from full speed after the World Cup, they are still some of the world’s best players and it was stirring to watch Villa youngsters Hemmings and Madjo going toe to toe with them.

Madjo's effort beat the goalkeeper for pace after he connected with a John McGinn cross

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia broke the deadlock with a lashed finish for French side

Hemmings was awarded an early free-kick by referee Omar Artan, the Somalian official who was denied entry to the United States ahead of the World Cup. Though Villa did not create anything from the free-kick, they had laid down a marker.

Even at half pace, PSG are incredibly dangerous when given a chance. After Marco Bizot had scooped away Desire Doue’s deflected shot, Madjo’s loose touch presented the ball to Vitinha. He found Doue and when Kvaratskhelia collected the ball, it was soon flying into the roof of the net from 15 yards.

Until then, Madjo had looked very raw and his technique needs refining – though there are few better coaches to do so than Emery. More importantly, he did not allow his head to drop and in the second part of the first half, PSG could not handle him.

Madjo headed two delightful crosses from McGinn over the bar, with the second a particularly bad miss. In between those chances, he had shot wide on an angle after more impressive work by Hemmings and seen another effort blocked following Emi Buendia’s run. Moments later, Madjo hit the outside of the post after holding off Pacho, though this was flagged offside onfield.

When Madjo did score, the opportunity was far tougher than those he had missed. From another McGinn cross, Madjo found his way on to the dangerous side of Pacho and volleyed beyond Matvei Safonov.

George Hemmings was another of the young Aston Villa stars lighting up the big stage

Unai Emery congratulates the PSG players after full time in Salzburg on Wednesday night

It was an uplifting end to the half for Villa, who deserved their equaliser. And soon after the break, they might have taken the lead. Madjo was involved again, this time taking a pass from Buendia and charging into space behind PSG’s high line.

He then fed McGinn, whose shot clipped Pacho and allowed Safonov a split second longer to make the save. Villa were still making the running though and just before the hour, Buendia headed over unmarked.

Against PSG, though, if you lose focus for the briefest moment you will be punished. Doue looked well offside when he took a pass from substitute Ousmane Dembele (not a bad player to be able bring on) and steered beyond Bizot.

The goal was ruled out on field but replays showed Matty Cash, half a yard behind the rest of Villa’s back four, had left Doue onside.

Back came Villa. Now it was Hemmings’ turn to break into the box and draw a save from Safonov. PSG were looking increasingly dangerous on the break but in the closing 10 minutes, Alysson could not find the return pass to give fellow substitute Tammy Abraham an easy equaliser.

Sports.title: Xavi appointed Netherlands head coach in shock move: Ex-Barcelona boss and former Man United target succeeds Ronald Koeman after Arne Slot turned job down
Sports.content:
Xavi appointed Netherlands head coach in shock move: Ex-Barcelona boss and former Man United target succeeds Ronald Koeman after Arne Slot turned job down

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Former Barcelona boss Xavi has been appointed the new head coach of the Netherlands.

The 46-year-old Spaniard has agreed a contract to lead the team through to the 2030 World Cup.

He replaces Ronald Koeman, who stepped down following the Netherlands' last-32 defeat by Morocco at this summer's World Cup.

Roberto Martinez was another name in the running, while ex-Liverpool boss Arne Slot withdrew from the race, citing his priority as remaining in the club game.

Former Barcelona midfielder Xavi won the World Cup as a player with Spain in 2010 and also lifted the European Championship in 2008 and 2012.

He guided Barcelona to the LaLiga title in 2023 after beginning his managerial career with Qatari club Al Sadd.

Xavi Hernandez has been appointed as the new Netherlands manager

'I consider it a tremendous honour to become head coach of the Dutch national team,' he said in a statement released by the Dutch Football Association (KNVB).

'As someone who received his training at the FC Barcelona academy, with strong influences from Johan Cruyff and Rinus Michels, among others, I feel a special connection to Dutch football.

'You could say that I am a bit of a son of Dutch football.'

Xavi’s appointment marks his first return to management since leaving Barcelona in 2024.

He took over the Catalan giants in November 2021, also succeeding Koeman, after making 767 appearances for the club.

'The Netherlands has a rich football culture and a clear vision that also appeals to me enormously: attacking football, based on possession, with creativity, passion, and conviction,' he continued.

'Of course, the most important goal is and always will be to win, but I prefer to do so in a way that reflects those characteristics and that people can enjoy.

'The potential for this is there, as well as a solid foundation to build upon.'

Explaining Xavi’s appointment, KNVB director of football Nigel de Jong said: 'As a coach, he has been shaped by years of working with top coaches who espouse a football vision that aligns very well with the way we want to play with the Dutch national team: taking initiative, dominant and attractive football, combined with the flexibility that modern elite football demands.

'Xavi believes in those basic principles, has embraced that vision, and made it his own. All of that, combined with his personality and the way he knows how to connect with players and get the best out of a group, makes him the right choice for the coming years.'

Sports.title: The encouraging signs emerging under Michael Carrick's coaching, Bryan Mbeumo passes latest No 9 audition - and the young star the club CANNOT afford to let go as Man United beat Leeds on penalties
Sports.content:
The encouraging signs emerging under Michael Carrick's coaching, Bryan Mbeumo passes latest No 9 audition - and the young star the club CANNOT afford to let go as Man United beat Leeds on penalties

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester United edged out rivals Leeds United on penalties to win the pre-season Boyle Sports Cup inside a sold-out Croke Park.

While the shootout - which almost didn't happen due to a deluge of young pitch invaders at full-time - ultimately separated the sides, both managers will have taken plenty from this pulsating clash under the lights in Dublin.

Bryan Mbeumo's audition to be Manchester United's starting striker for the opening game of the season was strengthened with another smart display, while Brenden Aaronson finished off a brilliant move to level things up at 1-1 in the first half.

James Justin's costly penalty miss as the fifth taker for Leeds allowed Noussair Mazraoui to win it with the final act as Michael Carrick's side clinched the game 5-4 on spot-kicks.

Daily Mail Sport brings you some of the biggest talking points from an historic night in Dublin…

Joshua Zirkzee (left) and Bryan Mbeumo (right) starred as Manchester United took on Leeds

TRUST COACH CARRICK

One of the things that Ruben Amorim called for was time on the training pitch to imprint his ideas on the United squad.

They fluffed the Europe league final to secure a season without European football and bar a couple of encouraging flashes, tangible signs of style and progress never materialised.

So to see Manchester United playing as well as they have throughout this pre-season - yes, it's pre-season - is a sign of just what good training ground coaches Carrick and his staff are proving to be.

It's a collective effort between Carrick, Steve Holland, Jonathan Woodgate, Jonny Evans, Travis Binnion, and many analysts in the background.

Here against Leeds United, much as it was against Paris Saint-Germain in Gothenburg last weekend, you can see tangible signs of progress in the way Carrick wants this team to evolve in its pressing and its play-style.

'He wants to have the ball, he wants to press in certain ways,' summer signing Youri Tielemans explained on Tuesday.

'It might be different than what you are used to, what I have been used to before, but it is logical things in my opinion. It is just smelling football, and that is what I have been doing from when I was young at Anderlecht, you know. So for me, nothing changes, but it just needs to gel together.'

United are proving a lot more aggressive in the press and the defensive work of Andrey Santos in midfield, one of the summer signings to the tune of £50million, is pivotal.

The encouraging thing is that while these haven't been perfect performances either, there are more first team stars to come back in.

United lit up Croke Park from the start without captain and talisman Bruno Fernandes, without Tielemans, without Matheus Cunha, without the returning Marcus Rashford, without Benjamin Sesko, and Matthijs de Ligt, and Harry Maguire.

The way Leeds picked United off, capitalising on loose control from Tyler Fletcher, shows that there is still work to do.

But stylistically United, visibly at least, appear to be getting better by the game. For Manchester United fans, that's an incredibly encouraging sign.

Throughout pre-season you can see exactly what Michael Carrick is trying to implement

MBEUMO ON A HEATER

In a summer at Manchester United which has been as much about evolution as it has been revolution, the results of the Bryan Mbeumo striker experiment are yielding some fascinating results.

The Cameroonian is far from a typical No 9 but for Michael Carrick and Manchester United's staff, that is a big part of his appeal.

There are a multitude of factors at play here. United want to platform academy star Shea Lacey for a full-time first team role and he predominantly plays off the right. There's also Amad, who is facing a defining season in that right-side role.

And then you add in that United only have one orthodox No 9 option in Benjamin Sesko, and he hasn't kicked a ball during pre-season due to an ongoing shin injury, although he did travel to Ireland to take part in this week-long training camp.

So Mbeumo as a striker, and a fluid one at that, holds great appeal and perhaps importance, should United not go and add another forward between now and the transfer deadline.

Mbeumo is going to start the season up top, that now looks clear, but expect Carrick to call upon Marcus Rashford, too.

'He's our player,' he said last night. 'He's come back great. He's just like any other player... He gives us something a little bit different.'

Mbeumo hit a real lull in front of goal in the second half of last season and struggled to rediscover momentum that had fans off their seats in the first half leading to question marks about how Carrick may get the best out of him.

But a brace against Atletico Madrid in Stockholm, the equaliser in Gothenburg against PSG, and a brilliant piece of skill, coupled with an assist, for Joshua Zirkzee to open the scoring here in Dublin showed just how much confidence is running through Mbeumo's veins right now.

For the opening goal here - and he should have had his own in the first half when he crashed a shot against the crossbar - he nutmegged two Leeds players as he burst down the left before playing Zirkzee through to score beyond new No 1 James Trafford.

Leeds went on to equalise through Brenden Aaronson in the first half and were good value for it after a rocky start. Despite Carrick's side dominating the ball when their main men came on, it finished 1-1 in front of an 82,000-strong sell-out crowd at Croke Park.

Mbeumo is set to start as centre forward against Hull City to kickstart the Premier League campaign and from there the sky really does feel like the limit for him. This is a formula now, not just an experiment.

TYNAN TIME

While he didn't quite get the loudest cheer of the night - that was reserved for the introduction of Bruno Fernandes off the bench - this was a huge milestone in the career of Tynan Thompson.

The 18-year-old arrived from Tottenham Hotspur this summer as an Emerging Talent Signing that Ineos and United's powers love, look at Ayden Heaven and numerous others.

This was Thompson's first taste of senior football at United and the first time he's been away and part of Carrick's group this pre-season.

Tynan Thompson got his first taste of senior football in a Manchester United shirt in Dublin

Thompson, who arrived in a deal that could eventually total £8m, got a pep talk from his manager moments before the second half restarted and the message, likely, was to be bold, be aggressive and have fun.

What we saw across 45 minutes was a player who looks unafraid to take people on and, in something of a quirk in the modern game, is a winger that likes to take people on on the outside.

A couple of times midway through the second half he managed to get down the left side with a quick burst and then drill a low cross in, only for Leeds to mop it up comfortably.

Sources at United won't pigeonhole Thompson as a first team player or an Under-21 player and he's likely to find himself straddling the two.

But don't underestimate the value of nights like these, in front of 82,000, with the likes of Fernandes and Cunha demanding the ball off you.

This isn't academy football any more…

HARRY'S STYLE

Speaking of rising stars, it should be an impossibility that Harry Amass is allowed to leave unless United go out and get another left back.

Sources have indicated that Amass has been told his best chance of regular minutes will come elsewhere and the club are unlikely to stand in his way for a loan or a permanent, if they get fair value.

That plan needs shelving immediately unless someone like Lewis Hall, who United have made two approaches for but failed on both occasions, walks through the door.

Amass may physically be on the smaller side in stature but he was dynamic in possession and fierce out of it here as Leeds looked to put him under real pressure, particularly early on before they clocked that they may be better off testing Diogo Dalot instead.

Amass has suitors aplenty should he walk out the door but with only Luke Shaw to call on as a bonafide left back right now, Amass should be staying until further notice.

There is no way Harry Amass can be allowed to leave without a new left back coming in

TRAFFORD IS TOP

One thing that Leeds do deserve credit for is the decisiveness they have shown in the goalkeeper department in getting a top talent in James Trafford.

They gave it as long as they could with Illan Meslier, then tried Lucas Perri out, and pivoted to Karl Darlow, now of Manchester United, before paying a club record £40m for him.

Officially Trafford got the Man of the Match here before it went to a penalty shootout and he did make a number of fine saves to keep Manchester United out, not least denying one effort from Zirkzee, and another from Mbeumo.

It cannot be understated just what a difference a truly top goalkeeper can make and if Leeds are to kick on like Brighton and Bournemouth did in getting into Europe, it is moves like Trafford that will go a long way to moving the needle.

MAKE IRELAND A YEARLY TRIP

Lastly, a sold out Croke Park was absolutely incredible, and a trip United should make yearly if the logistics were feasible.

The appetite for Manchester United in these parts is understandably huge and credit as well to the Leeds United contingent who travelled in good numbers.

Naturally the pre-season appeal is wherever the money is for Premier League clubs and the answer for Manchester United is often the United States.

But they could do a lot worse than secure themselves a near-enough home game in Ireland given how many fans turned out for this one.

A cracking trip that should give United's execs pause for thought.

Sports.title: Chelsea set Enzo Fernandez bid deadline: Blues tell Man City and other suitors to offer £120MILLION or forget about signing controversial Argentina star
Sports.content:
Chelsea set Enzo Fernandez bid deadline: Blues tell Man City and other suitors to offer £120MILLION or forget about signing controversial Argentina star

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Chelsea have told Manchester City they have until 5pm tomorrow to pay £120million to sign Enzo Fernandez — or forget about the transfer.

As Daily Mail Sport has reported previously in this window, City are interested in the Argentina midfielder, who shared a strong relationship with Enzo Maresca when he was Chelsea coach.

Fernandez, who returned to Chelsea training this week after helping his country to the World Cup final, has six years left on his contract.

If City do not meet Chelsea’s demands, the Stamford Bridge club do not intend to sell Fernandez in this window.

City’s interest in the player, 25, has been known to Chelsea since the end of last season which is when their valuation of the midfielder was confirmed to Fernandez’s agent, Javier Pastore.

Fernandez was one of the Argentina players who riled England after the ill-tempered World Cup semi-final in Atlanta, which Argentina won 2-1.

Manchester City have been handed a deadline of Thursday 5pm to bid for Enzo Fernandez

City boss Enzo Maresca is interested in bringing his former player to his new club

The Chelsea man drew Argentina level after 85 minutes and immediately raced over to stand in front of England fans, cupped his hands behind his ears and stuck out his tongue, then blew a kiss.

Chelsea were later forced to delete a post on X which celebrated wantaway star Fernandez’s equaliser after a furious response from fans up and down the country.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi says 'I don't know how to go on' and hints he will QUIT football as he breaks his silence on dad Jorge's death aged 68
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi says 'I don't know how to go on' and hints he will QUIT football as he breaks his silence on dad Jorge's death aged 68

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Cristiano Ronaldo paid tribute to the late father of his great rival, Lionel Messi, with a touching message on social media.

Lionel Messi has hinted he will retire from football following the devastating death of his father, Jorge, who was an integral figure in the career of his legendary son.

Jorge died on August 7 following a battle with illness that overshadowed the Argentina captain's mesmerising World Cup campaign in the United States, in which he led his team to the final.

Lionel, who broke down in tears following Argentina's group stage win over Algeria while Jorge's health was deteriorating, shared a heartbreaking letter to his father on Instagram – in which he casts doubt over his playing future.

'Dad, I still can't believe you're gone. It hasn't sunk in yet, or rather, I don't want to accept it. It's very difficult for me to imagine never seeing you again, never talking to you again. I know you were suffering and that this is for the best, but you left too soon. We still had so much to enjoy together.

'I don't know what I'll do without you, I don't know how to go on. I only played football and now I have serious doubts that I'll continue doing that for much longer. You were by my side from the beginning, it was so close to the end. Why couldn't you hold on that little bit longer and we could have finished together?'

Ronaldo replied to the post, saying: 'A huge hug to you and yours in these tough times, Leo. Much strength.'

The Portuguese legend knows of Messi's heartache only too well after losing his father, Jose Dinis Aveiro, in 2005 to an alcoholism-related live condition when he was aged just 20.

'I really don’t know my father 100 per cent,' Ronaldo told Piers Morgan in 2019. 'He was a drunk person. I never spoke with him, like a normal conversation. It was hard.'

Messi revealed that his father was the driving force behind his decision to play at this summer's World Cup, but his ageing legs prevented him from bringing the trophy home – with Spain winning 1-0 in the New York final.

Lionel Messi has thanked fans for their support following the death of his father Jorge (left)

Messi's father and agent died in Rosario, Argentina on Friday August 7

Jorge's death saw an outpouring of emotional tributes from the football world, including from Messi's first team Newell's Old Boys, as well as Barcelona and Argentina.

'You kept asking me to play in the last World Cup, and just a few days before it started, you got worse. It was the first time you wouldn't be in a tournament, but Mom kept telling me you'd get better and be well enough to travel. I told you we were going to reach the final so you could travel.

'Every time a game ended, I waited and missed your message. That's when I realized the situation was really serious. Even so, I couldn't stop thinking about going as far as possible, to give you time and for you to see a game. We reached the final and you couldn't be there. I wanted to win it to bring it to you and show you a new one. I couldn't, my legs couldn't take it anymore. This time I tried to go against my physical limitations, but I couldn't. I never managed to feel well.

'When I arrived, you thought we'd lost the final on penalties. We couldn't talk about anything that happened. You couldn't enjoy any of it. We didn't win the championship, but you don't know how much we enjoyed every game. Once again, you were right: I had to be there and play.

'I'm telling you this because it was the only thing we couldn't talk about, because you already know everything else. We used to talk every day and see each other whenever possible, given my commitments.'

Messi missed Inter Miami's defeat by Monterrey on Sunday to return home in the wake of his father's passing, and thanked fans for their well wishes.

He added on his Instagram stories: 'I want to sincerely thank everyone for all the love, respect and enormous consideration you have shown me and my family during this incredibly painful time following the loss of my dad.

'Thank you for being there for us, for every message, every gesture and, above all, for respecting our grief and our privacy.'

Lionel Messi's father Jorge, pictured at the 2022 World Cup final, died at the age of 68

MESSI STATEMENT IN FULL 'Dad, I still can't believe you're gone. It hasn't sunk in yet, or rather, I don't want to accept it. It's very difficult for me to imagine never seeing you again, never talking to you again. I know you were suffering and that this is for the best, but you left too soon. We still had so much to enjoy together.' You kept asking me to play in the last World Cup, and just a few days before it started, you got worse. It was the first time you wouldn't be in a tournament, but Mom kept telling me you'd get better and be well enough to travel. I told you we were going to reach the final so you could travel. Every time a game ended, I waited and missed your message. That's when I realized the situation was really serious. Even so, I couldn't stop thinking about going as far as possible, to give you time and for you to see a game. We reached the final and you couldn't be there. I wanted to win it to bring it to you and show you a new one. I couldn't, my legs couldn't take it anymore. This time I tried to go against my physical limitations, but I couldn't. I never managed to feel well. When I arrived, you thought we'd lost the final on penalties. We couldn't talk about anything that happened. You couldn't enjoy any of it. We didn't win the championship, but you don't know how much we enjoyed every game. Once again, you were right: I had to be there and play. I'm telling you this because it was the only thing we couldn't talk about, because you already know everything else. We used to talk every day and see each other whenever possible, given my commitments. I don't know what I'll do without you, I don't know how to go on. I only played football and now I have serious doubts that I'll continue doing that for much longer. You were by my side from the beginning, it was so close to the end. Why couldn't you hold on that little bit longer and we could have finished together? I know that his happiness was seeing his family well, his wife, his children and, above all, without others knowing, seeing me play. It's always been like this since I was little. You'd take me to all the practices as soon as you got home from work. Many times, Mom would take me because you were working. Obviously, you never missed a game. How you suffered watching me, and how you enjoyed it, even though you never gave me many compliments. You were a father, a friend, and a businessman. You were always the person you needed to be in every situation and you never made a mistake. Aside from a few demands or arguments, you were always right. In the end, things always turned out exactly as you said. I will miss you very much, but you will always be present, especially in the upbringing of my children, because I teach and educate them as you did with me. Rest in peace and watch over us from up there as you did here. Thank you for everything. I love you, Dad.

Messi also posted a picture with his father, captioned: 'I love you, pa' in Spanish.

Football legend Messi was extremely close to his father, who also operated as his agent and de facto business manager throughout his career, overseeing his son's multi-million dollar empire off the pitch.

In recent months, though, the patriarch of the family had been dealing with an as-yet-unconfirmed medical issue that had seen him taken to hospital in his home country.

His illness first came to light when Lionel, 39, cried on the pitch at the World Cup in a rare public display of emotion.

After scoring a hat-trick against Algeria in Argentina's opening group game in Kansas City, Messi was questioned by journalists and said: 'No, honestly it's something completely unrelated to sports. It's been a few difficult days, complicated.'

Just hours later, journalist Eduardo Feinmann explained the reason for the tears in an interview on Radio Mitre, one of the country's most listened-to stations.

'This has to do with his father. His father is not in good health,' he said. 'For quite some time now, several months, since last year.

'And this week there were some situations that slightly worsened his health, and Messi is going through this internal struggle. In other words, like any human being.'

It has since been reported that Jorge suffered a 'medical episode' at his home in January of this year, and he was hospitalised as a result.

In the aftermath, he was said to have undergone cardiovascular and neurological tests, but no official diagnosis was shared by the family, who sought to keep Jorge's health out of the media.

Jorge's health became headline news again in June, when a broadcaster in Argentina falsely claimed he had died – before later issuing an emotional apology and stepping down from her job.

Lionel is the third of four children of Jorge and his wife Celia Cuccittini, and the pair remained together until his death.

They married in 1978 and split their time between Rosario and Miami, where their footballing superstar son currently plays for David Beckham's Inter Miami in Major League Soccer (MLS).

Before becoming Lionel's agent, Jorge worked for a steel manufacturer in Villa Constitucion, meeting his wife as a young man in Rosario – where the family then grew up.

Messi stands in front of his family (including father Jorge (third left) in Rosario in October 2003

Jorge arrives at son Lionel's wedding in 2017 with his wife Celia (L) and daughter Maria (R)

Messi has two older brothers, Rodrigo and Matias, and a younger sister, Maria Sol.

Jorge has been at Messi's side throughout his historic career, which began in Argentina with Newell's Old Boys, before he moved to Spain to join Barcelona's famed La Masia academy in 2000.

He became the greatest of all-time in an incredible 21 years in Barcelona, before stunning the world with a move to Paris Saint-Germain – orchestrated by Jorge – in 2021.

After two seasons in the French capital, he moved to MLS and Inter Miami, where he remains to this day at the age of 39.

While Lionel's career has been magical on the pitch, it has not been without controversy off it, with Jorge famously by his son's side throughout his tax fraud case in 2016.

The pair sat together in front of the court, with Jorge in his role as his son's business manager, with the prosecution alleging that Messi failed to properly pay tax on income from his image rights between 2007 and 2009.

Ultimately, both father and son were convicted of three tax offenses, initially each receiving suspended 21-month prison sentences.

Jorge's sentence was subsequently reduced to 15 months upon review in 2017 by Spain's Supreme Court, with the pair also hit with substantial fines.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
